16.20.s:
.. īśvara uvāca .. ..
atha daityāvatārāṇāṃ kramo hi kathyate punaḥ ..
hiraṇyakaśipū rājā varṣāṇāmarbudaṃ babhau .. 1 ..
16.20.d:
.. ईश्वर उवाच .. ..
अथ दैत्यावताराणां क्रमो हि कथ्यते पुनः ..
हिरण्यकशिपू राजा वर्षाणामर्बुदं बभौ .. 1 ..
16.20.m: Īśvara said: / Now the order of the daitya descents is recounted again. / King Hiraṇyakaśipu reigned for a hundred million years.

16.20.s:
tathā śata sahasrāṇi yāni kāni dvisaptatim ..
aśītiṃ ca sahasrāṇi trailokyasyeśvaro'bhavat..2..
16.20.d:
तथा शत सहस्राणि यानि कानि द्विसप्ततिम् ..
अशीतिं च सहस्राणि त्रैलोक्यस्येश्वरोऽभवत्..2..
16.20.m: Likewise, for some seventy-two hundred thousand / and eighty thousand years, he was lord of the three worlds.

16.20.s: sautye'hanyatirātrasya kaśyapasyāśvamedhike ..3..
16.20.d: सौत्येऽहन्यतिरात्रस्य कश्यपस्याश्वमेधिके ..3..
16.20.m: On the day of the Soma pressing during the Atirātra in the Aśvamedha of Kaśyapa,

16.20.s:
upakṣiptā sanaṃ yattu hoturarthe hiraṇmayam ..
niṣasāda sa garto(?)'tra hiraṇyakaśipustataḥ .. 4 ..
16.20.d:
उपक्षिप्ता सनं यत्तु होतुरर्थे हिरण्मयम् ..
निषसाद स गर्तो(?)ऽत्र हिरण्यकशिपुस्ततः .. 4 ..
16.20.m: the golden seat that was placed there for the Hotṛ priest— / there Hiraṇyakaśipu sat down on that seat.

16.20.s:
śatavarṣasahasrāṇāṃ tapaścakre suduścaram ..
daśavarṣasahasrāṇi dityā garbhe sthitaḥ purā .. 5 ..
16.20.d:
शतवर्षसहस्राणां तपश्चक्रे सुदुश्चरम् ..
दशवर्षसहस्राणि दित्या गर्भे स्थितः पुरा .. 5 ..
16.20.m: He performed extremely arduous austerity for a hundred thousand years; / previously, he had remained in Diti's womb for ten thousand years.

16.20.s:
hiraṇyakaśipordaityaḥ śloko gītaḥ purātanaḥ ..
rājā hiraṇyakaśipuryāṃ yāmāśāṃ nirīkṣate .. 6 ..
16.20.d:
हिरण्यकशिपोर्दैत्यः श्लोको गीतः पुरातनः ..
राजा हिरण्यकशिपुर्यां यामाशां निरीक्षते .. 6 ..
16.20.m: An ancient verse is sung regarding the daitya Hiraṇyakaśipu: / 'Whichever direction King Hiraṇyakaśipu looks upon,

16.20.s:
tasyāṃ tasyāṃ diśi surā namaścakruḥ saharṣibhiḥ 1.
paryāye tasya rājābhūdbalirvarṣārbudaṃ punaḥ .. 7 ..
16.20.d:
तस्यां तस्यां दिशि सुरा नमश्चक्रुः सहर्षिभिः 1.
पर्याये तस्य राजाभूद्बलिर्वर्षार्बुदं पुनः .. 7 ..
16.20.m: in that very direction the gods bowed along with the seers.' / In his turn, Bali again became king for a hundred million years,

16.20.s:
ṣaṣṭiṃ caiva sahasrāṇi triṃśacca niyutāni ca ..
bale rājyādhikārastu yāva tkālaṃ babhūva ha .. 8 ..
16.20.d:
षष्टिं चैव सहस्राणि त्रिंशच्च नियुतानि च ..
बले राज्याधिकारस्तु याव त्कालं बभूव ह .. 8 ..
16.20.m: and sixty thousand and thirty million years— / for that long Bali's sovereign rule lasted.

16.20.s:
prahlādo nigṛhīto'bhūttāvatkālaṃ tathā suraiḥ 1.
iṃdrādayaste vikhyātā asurāñjaghnurojasā .. 9 ..
16.20.d:
प्रह्लादो निगृहीतोऽभूत्तावत्कालं तथा सुरैः 1.
इंद्रादयस्ते विख्याता असुराञ्जघ्नुरोजसा .. 9 ..
16.20.m: Prahlāda was restrained by the gods during that time; / Indra and the other celebrated ones slew the asuras with their might.

16.20.s:
daityasaṃsthamidaṃ sarvamā sīddaśayugaṃ kila ..
asapatnaṃ tataḥ sarvamaṣṭādaśayugaṃ punaḥ .. 7.1.20.10 ..
16.20.d:
दैत्यसंस्थमिदं सर्वमा सीद्दशयुगं किल ..
असपत्नं ततः सर्वमष्टादशयुगं पुनः .. 7.1.20.10 ..
16.20.m: All this was held by the daityas for ten yugas, they say; / thereafter, it was entirely without rival for eighteen yugas again.

16.20.s:
trailokyamidamavyagraṃ maheṃdreṇa tu pālitam ..
tretāyuge tu daśame kārttavīryo mahābalaḥ .. 11 ..
16.20.d:
त्रैलोक्यमिदमव्यग्रं महेंद्रेण तु पालितम् ..
त्रेतायुगे तु दशमे कार्त्तवीर्यो महाबलः .. 11 ..
16.20.m: This threefold world was ruled unperturbed by Mahendra. / In the tenth Tretāyuga, the mighty Kārttavīrya [arose],

16.20.s:
paṃcāśītisahasrāṇi varṣāṇāṃ vai narādhipaḥ ..
sa saptaratnavānsamrāṭ cakravartī babhūva ha .. 12 ..
16.20.d:
पंचाशीतिसहस्राणि वर्षाणां वै नराधिपः ..
स सप्तरत्नवान्सम्राट् चक्रवर्ती बभूव ह .. 12 ..
16.20.m: a king of men for eighty-five thousand years; / possessing the seven jewels, he was an emperor and universal monarch.

16.20.s:
dvīpeṣu saptasu sa vai khaḍgī carmī śarāsanī ..
rathī rājā sānucaro yogāccaurānapaśyata .. 13 ..
16.20.d:
द्वीपेषु सप्तसु स वै खड्गी चर्मी शरासनी ..
रथी राजा सानुचरो योगाच्चौरानपश्यत .. 13 ..
16.20.m: Bearing sword, shield, and bow, riding a chariot, / that king with his retinue perceived thieves through yoga across the seven continents.

16.20.s:
praṇaṣṭadravyatā yasya smaraṇānna bhavennṛṇām ..
caturyuge tvatikrāṃte manau hyekādaśe prabhau .. 14 ..
16.20.d:
प्रणष्टद्रव्यता यस्य स्मरणान्न भवेन्नृणाम् ..
चतुर्युगे त्वतिक्रांते मनौ ह्येकादशे प्रभौ .. 14 ..
16.20.m: Men never suffer the loss of property merely by remembering him. / When four yugas had passed in the reign of the eleventh sovereign Manu,

16.20.s:
arddhāvaśiṣṭe tasmiṃstu dvāpare saṃpravartite ..
mānavasya nariṣyaṃto hyāsītputro madaḥ kila ... .. 15 ..
16.20.d:
अर्द्धावशिष्टे तस्मिंस्तु द्वापरे संप्रवर्तिते ..
मानवस्य नरिष्यंतो ह्यासीत्पुत्रो मदः किल ... .. 15 ..
16.20.m: when that Dvāpara had proceeded with half remaining, / the son of Nariṣyanta, son of Manu, was indeed Mada.

16.20.s:
navamastasya dāyādastṛṇabiṃduriti smṛtaḥ ..
tretāyugamukhe rājā tṛtīye saṃbabhūva ha .. 16 ..
16.20.d:
नवमस्तस्य दायादस्तृणबिंदुरिति स्मृतः ..
त्रेतायुगमुखे राजा तृतीये संबभूव ह .. 16 ..
16.20.m: His ninth descendant was known as Tṛṇabindu; / at the beginning of the third Tretāyuga he was born as king.

16.20.s:
tasya kanyā tvilavilā rūpe ṇāpratimā'bhavat ..
pulastyāya sa rājarṣistāṃ kanyāṃ pratyapādayat .. 17 ..
16.20.d:
तस्य कन्या त्विलविला रूपे णाप्रतिमाऽभवत् ..
पुलस्त्याय स राजर्षिस्तां कन्यां प्रत्यपादयत् .. 17 ..
16.20.m: His daughter, however, was Ilavilā, who was peerless in beauty. / That royal sage gave that daughter in marriage to Pulastya.

16.20.s:
ṛṣirailavilo yasyāṃ viśravāḥ samapadyata ..
tasya patnyaśca tisrastu paulastyakulamaṃḍanāḥ .. 18 ..
16.20.d:
ऋषिरैलविलो यस्यां विश्रवाः समपद्यत ..
तस्य पत्न्यश्च तिस्रस्तु पौलस्त्यकुलमंडनाः .. 18 ..
16.20.m: From her was born the seer Viśravas, son of Ilavilā. / He had three wives who adorned the lineage of Pulastya:

16.20.s:
bṛhaspateḥ śubhā kanyā nāmnā vai vedavarṇinī ..
puṣpotkaṭā ca vīkā ca ubhe mālyavataḥ sute .. 19 ..
16.20.d:
बृहस्पतेः शुभा कन्या नाम्ना वै वेदवर्णिनी ..
पुष्पोत्कटा च वीका च उभे माल्यवतः सुते .. 19 ..
16.20.m: The auspicious daughter of Bṛhaspati named Vedavarṇinī, / and Puṣpotkaṭā and Vīkā, both daughters of Mālyavat.

16.20.s:
kekasī mālinaḥ kanyā tasyāṃ devi śṛṇu prajāḥ ..
jyeṣṭhaṃ vaiśravaṇaṃ tasya suṣuve varavarṇinī .. 7.1.20.20 ..
16.20.d:
केकसी मालिनः कन्या तस्यां देवि शृणु प्रजाः ..
ज्येष्ठं वैश्रवणं तस्य सुषुवे वरवर्णिनी .. 7.1.20.20 ..
16.20.m: Kekasī was the daughter of Mālin; hear, O goddess, about the offspring born from her. / That fair-complexioned woman bore to him her eldest son, Vaiśravaṇa,

16.20.s:
aṣṭadaṃ(?) haricchmaśruṃ śaṃkukarṇaṃ vilohitam ..
śvapādaṃ hrasvabāhuṃ ca piṃgalaṃ śucibhūṣaṇam .. 21 ..
16.20.d:
अष्टदं(?) हरिच्छ्मश्रुं शंकुकर्णं विलोहितम् ..
श्वपादं ह्रस्वबाहुं च पिंगलं शुचिभूषणम् .. 21 ..
16.20.m: having eight teeth, a yellowish beard, peg-like ears, and a reddish hue, / with dog-like feet, short arms, tawny-eyed, adorned with pure ornaments,

16.20.s:
tripādaṃ tu mahākāyaṃ sthūlaśīrṣaṃ mahāhanum ..
evaṃvidhaṃ sutaṃ dṛṣṭvā virūpaṃ rūpatastadā .. 22..
16.20.d:
त्रिपादं तु महाकायं स्थूलशीर्षं महाहनुम् ..
एवंविधं सुतं दृष्ट्वा विरूपं रूपतस्तदा .. 22..
16.20.m: having three legs, a huge body, a thick head, and large jaws. / Seeing such a son, deformed in his appearance,

16.20.s:
tadā dṛṣṭvābravīttaṃ tu kubero'yamiti svayam..
kutsāyāṃ kvitiśabdoyaṃ śarīraṃ veramucyate .. 23 ..
16.20.d:
तदा दृष्ट्वाब्रवीत्तं तु कुबेरोऽयमिति स्वयम्..
कुत्सायां क्वितिशब्दोयं शरीरं वेरमुच्यते .. 23 ..
16.20.m: he himself, upon seeing him then, said: 'This is Kubera.' / The word 'ku' is used in contempt, and the body is called 'bera';

16.20.s:
kuberaḥ kuśarīratvānnāmnā tena ca soṃkitaḥ ..
tasya bhāryyā'bhavadvṛddhiḥ putrastu nalakūbaraḥ .. 24 ..
16.20.d:
कुबेरः कुशरीरत्वान्नाम्ना तेन च सोंकितः ..
तस्य भार्य्याऽभवद्वृद्धिः पुत्रस्तु नलकूबरः .. 24 ..
16.20.m: because he possessed an ugly body, he was marked by that name 'Kubera.' / His wife was Vṛddhi, and his son was Nalakūbara.

16.20.s:
kaikasyajanayatputraṃ rāvaṇaṃ rākṣasādhipam ..
śaṃkukarṇaṃ daśagrīvaṃ pigalaṃ raktamūrddhajam.. 25 ..
16.20.d:
कैकस्यजनयत्पुत्रं रावणं राक्षसाधिपम् ..
शंकुकर्णं दशग्रीवं पिगलं रक्तमूर्द्धजम्.. 25 ..
16.20.m: Kekasī gave birth to a son, Rāvaṇa, the lord of the rākṣasas, / having peg-like ears, ten necks, tawny-eyed, and with red hair,

16.20.s:
vasupādaṃ viṃśadbhujaṃ mahākāyaṃ mahābalam ..
kālāṃjananibhaṃ caiva daṃṣṭriṇaṃ raktalocanam .. 26 ..
16.20.d:
वसुपादं विंशद्भुजं महाकायं महाबलम् ..
कालांजननिभं चैव दंष्ट्रिणं रक्तलोचनम् .. 26 ..
16.20.m: having eight feet, twenty arms, a huge body, and immense strength, / resembling black collyrium, having fangs, and red eyes,

16.20.s:
rākṣasenaujasā yuktaṃ rūpeṇa ca balena ca ..
nisargāddāruṇaḥ krūro rāvaṇādrāvaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ ..27..
16.20.d:
राक्षसेनौजसा युक्तं रूपेण च बलेन च ..
निसर्गाद्दारुणः क्रूरो रावणाद्रावणः स्मृतः ..27..
16.20.m: endowed with the fiery energy, form, and strength of a rākṣasa. / Fierce and cruel by nature, he was called Rāvaṇa because of his causing lamentation.

16.20.s:
hiraṇyakaśipustvāsītsa rājā pūrvajanmani ..
caturyugāni rājā tu tathā daśa sa rākṣasaḥ ..28..
16.20.d:
हिरण्यकशिपुस्त्वासीत्स राजा पूर्वजन्मनि ..
चतुर्युगानि राजा तु तथा दश स राक्षसः ..28..
16.20.m: In his previous birth, that rākṣasa had indeed been King Hiraṇyakaśipu. / As a king and as a rākṣasa, he ruled for fourteen caturyugas:

16.20.s:
paṃca koṭīstu varṣāṇāṃ saṃkhyatāḥ saṃkhyāyā priye ..
niyutānyekaṣaṣṭiṃ ca saṃkhyāvadbhirudāhṛtam .. 29 ..
16.20.d:
पंच कोटीस्तु वर्षाणां संख्यताः संख्याया प्रिये ..
नियुतान्येकषष्टिं च संख्यावद्भिरुदाहृतम् .. 29 ..
16.20.m: fifty million years have been computed by count, O beloved, / and sixty-one hundred-thousands, as stated by the reckoners,

16.20.s:
ṣaṣṭiṃ caiva sahasrāṇi varṣāṇāṃ sa hi rāvaṇaḥ ..
devatānāmṛṣīṇāṃ ca ghoraṃ kṛtvā prajāgaram .. 7.1.20.30 ..
16.20.d:
षष्टिं चैव सहस्राणि वर्षाणां स हि रावणः ..
देवतानामृषीणां च घोरं कृत्वा प्रजागरम् .. 7.1.20.30 ..
16.20.m: and also sixty thousand years—for that long, indeed, Rāvaṇa / kept up a terrible vigil of harassment against the gods and the seers.

16.20.s:
tretāyuge caturviṃśe rāvaṇastapasaḥ kṣayāt ..
rāmaṃ dāśarathiṃ prāpya sagaṇaḥ kṣayameyivān .. 31 ..
16.20.d:
त्रेतायुगे चतुर्विंशे रावणस्तपसः क्षयात् ..
रामं दाशरथिं प्राप्य सगणः क्षयमेयिवान् .. 31 ..
16.20.m: In the twenty-fourth Tretāyuga, on account of the exhaustion of his austerity, / Rāvaṇa encountered Rāma, son of Daśaratha, and went to destruction along with his host.

16.20.s:
yo'sau devi daśagrīvaḥ saṃbabhūvārimarddanaḥ ..
damaghoṣasya rājarṣeḥ putro vikhyātapauruṣaḥ ..32..
16.20.d:
योऽसौ देवि दशग्रीवः संबभूवारिमर्द्दनः ..
दमघोषस्य राजर्षेः पुत्रो विख्यातपौरुषः ..32..
16.20.m: He who was the ten-necked crusher of foes, O goddess, / was reborn as the son of the royal sage Damaghoṣa, renowned for his manly valour,

16.20.s:
śrutaśravāyāṃ caidyastu śiśupālo babhūva ha ..
rāvaṇaṃ kuṃbhakarṇaṃ ca kanyāṃ śūrpaṇakhāṃ tathā ..33..
16.20.d:
श्रुतश्रवायां चैद्यस्तु शिशुपालो बभूव ह ..
रावणं कुंभकर्णं च कन्यां शूर्पणखां तथा ..33..
16.20.m: born of Śrutaśravā as the Caidya prince Śiśupāla. / Kekasī gave birth to Rāvaṇa, Kumbhakarṇa, and a daughter, Śūrpaṇakhā,

16.20.s:
vibhīṣaṇaṃ caturthaṃ ca kaikasyajanayatsutān ..
manoharaḥ prahastaśca mahāpārśvaḥ kharastathā ..34..
16.20.d:
विभीषणं चतुर्थं च कैकस्यजनयत्सुतान् ..
मनोहरः प्रहस्तश्च महापार्श्वः खरस्तथा ..34..
16.20.m: and Vibhīṣaṇa as the fourth son. / Manohara, Prahasta, Mahāpārśva, and Khara—

16.20.s:
puṣpotkaṭāyāste putrāḥ kanyā kumbhīnasī tathā ..
triśirā dūṣaṇaścaiva vidyujjihvaśca rākṣasaḥ..
kanyaikā śyāmikā nāma vīkāyāḥ prasavaḥ smṛtaḥ..35..
16.20.d:
पुष्पोत्कटायास्ते पुत्राः कन्या कुम्भीनसी तथा ..
त्रिशिरा दूषणश्चैव विद्युज्जिह्वश्च राक्षसः..
कन्यैका श्यामिका नाम वीकायाः प्रसवः स्मृतः..35..
16.20.m: these were the sons of Puṣpotkaṭā, and Kumbhīnasī was her daughter. / Triśiras, Dūṣaṇa, and the rākṣasa Vidyujjihva, / and one daughter named Śyāmikā, are recorded as the offspring of Vīkā.

16.20.s:
ityete krūrakarmāṇaḥ paulastyā rākṣasā nava ..
vibhīṣaṇo viśuddhātmā daśamaḥ parikīrtitaḥ ..36..
16.20.d:
इत्येते क्रूरकर्माणः पौलस्त्या राक्षसा नव ..
विभीषणो विशुद्धात्मा दशमः परिकीर्तितः ..36..
16.20.m: Thus, these nine descendants of Pulastya were rākṣasas of cruel deeds; / Vibhīṣaṇa, pure in mind, is proclaimed as the tenth.

16.20.s:
pulahasya mṛgāḥ putrāḥ sarve vyālāśca daṃṣṭriṇaḥ ..
bhūtāḥ piśācāḥ sarpāśca śūkarā hastinastathā .. ..37..
16.20.d:
पुलहस्य मृगाः पुत्राः सर्वे व्यालाश्च दंष्ट्रिणः ..
भूताः पिशाचाः सर्पाश्च शूकरा हस्तिनस्तथा .. ..37..
16.20.m: The sons of Pulaha were all deer, carnivorous beasts with fangs, / bhūtas, piśācas, serpents, boars, and elephants.

16.20.s:
anapatyaḥ kratustvasminsmṛto vaivasvateṃtare ..
atreḥ patnyo daśaivāsansundaryaśca pativratāḥ ..38..
16.20.d:
अनपत्यः क्रतुस्त्वस्मिन्स्मृतो वैवस्वतेंतरे ..
अत्रेः पत्न्यो दशैवासन्सुन्दर्यश्च पतिव्रताः ..38..
16.20.m: Kratu, however, is remembered as childless in this Vaivasvata Manvantara. / Atri had ten wives, all beautiful and devoted to their husband.

16.20.s: bhadrāśvasya ghṛtācyaṃtā jajñire daśa cāpsarāḥ ..39..
16.20.d: भद्राश्वस्य घृताच्यंता जज्ञिरे दश चाप्सराः ..39..
16.20.m: From Bhadrāśva and ending with Ghṛtācī, ten apsarases were born:

16.20.s:
bhadrā śūdrā ca madrā ca naladā jaladā tathā ..
urṇā pūrṇā ca deveśi yā ca gopucchalā smṛtā..7.1.20.40..
16.20.d:
भद्रा शूद्रा च मद्रा च नलदा जलदा तथा ..
उर्णा पूर्णा च देवेशि या च गोपुच्छला स्मृता..7.1.20.40..
16.20.m: Bhadrā, Śūdrā, Madrā, Naladā, Jaladā, / Urṇā, Pūrṇā, and, O ruler of the gods, she who is known as Gopucchalā,

16.20.s:
tathā tāmarasā nāma daśamī raktakoṭikā ..
etāsāṃ ca mahādevi khyāto bharttā prabhākaraḥ .. 41 ..
16.20.d:
तथा तामरसा नाम दशमी रक्तकोटिका ..
एतासां च महादेवि ख्यातो भर्त्ता प्रभाकरः .. 41 ..
16.20.m: and also the one named Tāmarasā, and the tenth, Raktakoṭikā. / Their renowned husband, O great goddess, was Prabhākara.

16.20.s:
svarbhānunā hate sūrye patitesmindivo mahīm ..
tamo'bhibhūte lokesminprabhā yena pravarttitā ..! .. 42 ..
16.20.d:
स्वर्भानुना हते सूर्ये पतितेस्मिन्दिवो महीम् ..
तमोऽभिभूते लोकेस्मिन्प्रभा येन प्रवर्त्तिता ..! .. 42 ..
16.20.m: When the sun was struck down by Svarbhānu and fell from heaven to this earth, / he by whom light was restored when this world was overcome by darkness,

16.20.s:
svasti testviti caivoktaḥ patanniha divākaraḥ ..
brahmarṣervacanāttasya na papāta yataḥ prabhuḥ .. 43 ..
16.20.d:
स्वस्ति तेस्त्विति चैवोक्तः पतन्निह दिवाकरः ..
ब्रह्मर्षेर्वचनात्तस्य न पपात यतः प्रभुः .. 43 ..
16.20.m: and to the sun as it was falling down here, it was said, 'May it be well with you!' / and by the word of that brahmin seer, the lord did not fall—

16.20.s:
tataḥ prabhākaretyuktaḥ prabhurevaṃ maharṣibhiḥ ..
bhadrāyāṃ janayāmām somaṃ putraṃ yaśasvinam .. 44 ..
16.20.d:
ततः प्रभाकरेत्युक्तः प्रभुरेवं महर्षिभिः ..
भद्रायां जनयामाम् सोमं पुत्रं यशस्विनम् .. 44 ..
16.20.m: therefore that lord was called 'Prabhākara' ('maker of light') by the great seers. / On Bhadrā he begat a glorious son, Soma,

16.20.s:
tviṣimāndharmaputrastu somo devo varastu saḥ ..
śītaraśmiḥ samutpannaḥ kṛttikāsu niśācaraḥ.. .45..
16.20.d:
त्विषिमान्धर्मपुत्रस्तु सोमो देवो वरस्तु सः ..
शीतरश्मिः समुत्पन्नः कृत्तिकासु निशाचरः.. .45..
16.20.m: who was radiant, a son of Dharma, the excellent god Soma, / the cool-rayed night-wanderer, who arose among the Kṛttikās.

16.20.s:
pitā somasya vai devi jajñe'trirbhagavānṛṣiḥ ..
tatrātriḥ sarvalokeśaṃ bhṛtvā sve nayane sthitaḥ .. 46 ..
16.20.d:
पिता सोमस्य वै देवि जज्ञेऽत्रिर्भगवानृषिः ..
तत्रात्रिः सर्वलोकेशं भृत्वा स्वे नयने स्थितः .. 46 ..
16.20.m: The father of Soma, O goddess, was known to be the venerable seer Atri. / There Atri, having held the lord of all worlds, remained in his own eyes.

16.20.s:
karmaṇā manasā vācā śubhānyeva samā carat ..
kāṣṭhakuḍyaśilābhūta ūrddhvabāhurmahādyutiḥ ..47..
16.20.d:
कर्मणा मनसा वाचा शुभान्येव समा चरत् ..
काष्ठकुड्यशिलाभूत ऊर्द्ध्वबाहुर्महाद्युतिः ..47..
16.20.m: In action, mind, and speech he practiced only auspicious things. / Becoming like a piece of wood, a wall, or a stone, with arms raised high, possessed of great splendor,

16.20.s:
sudustaraṃ nāma tapastena taptaṃ mahatpurā ..
trīṇi varṣasahasrāṇi divyāni surasuṃdari .. 48 ..
16.20.d:
सुदुस्तरं नाम तपस्तेन तप्तं महत्पुरा ..
त्रीणि वर्षसहस्राणि दिव्यानि सुरसुंदरि .. 48 ..
16.20.m: great austerity named Sudustara ('most difficult to perform') was practiced by him of old / for three thousand divine years, O beauty of the gods.

16.20.s:
tasyorddhvaretasastatra sthitasyānimiṣasya ha ..
somatvaṃ vapurāpede mahābuddhestu vai śubhe .. 49 ..
16.20.d:
तस्योर्द्ध्वरेतसस्तत्र स्थितस्यानिमिषस्य ह ..
सोमत्वं वपुरापेदे महाबुद्धेस्तु वै शुभे .. 49 ..
16.20.m: For him who had sublimated his virility, standing there without blinking, / the body of that one of great intellect attained the state of Soma, O auspicious one.

16.20.s:
ūrddhvamācakrame tasya somasaṃbhāvitātmanaḥ ..
netrābhyāṃ somaḥ susrāva daśadhā dyotayandiśaḥ .. 7.1.20.50 ..
16.20.d:
ऊर्द्ध्वमाचक्रमे तस्य सोमसंभावितात्मनः ..
नेत्राभ्यां सोमः सुस्राव दशधा द्योतयन्दिशः .. 7.1.20.50 ..
16.20.m: The semen of him whose self had become Soma mounted upward; / from his eyes Soma flowed forth, illuminating the ten directions.

16.20.s:
tadgarbhaṃ vidhinā dṛṣṭā diśodaśa dadhustadā ..
sametya dhārayāmāsurna ca dhartumaśaknuvan .. .. 51 ..
16.20.d:
तद्गर्भं विधिना दृष्टा दिशोदश दधुस्तदा ..
समेत्य धारयामासुर्न च धर्तुमशक्नुवन् .. .. 51 ..
16.20.m: Seeing that embryo according to the cosmic ordinance, the ten directions then conceived it; / coming together, they bore it, but they were not able to hold it.

16.20.s: sa tābhyaḥ sahasaiveha digbhyo garbhaśca śāśvataḥ .. papāta bhāvayam̐llokāñchītāṃśuḥ sarvabhāvanaḥ .. 52 ..
16.20.d: स ताभ्यः सहसैवेह दिग्भ्यो गर्भश्च शाश्वतः .. पपात भावयम्̐ल्लोकाञ्छीतांशुः सर्वभावनः .. 52 ..
16.20.m: That eternal embryo fell suddenly from those directions to this earth, / the cool-rayed one who brings life to all, causing the worlds to flourish.

16.20.s:
yadā na dhāraṇe śaktāstasya garbhasya tāḥ striyaḥ ..
tatastābhyaḥ sa śītāṃśurnipapāta vasuṃdharām .. 53 ..
16.20.d:
यदा न धारणे शक्तास्तस्य गर्भस्य ताः स्त्रियः ..
ततस्ताभ्यः स शीतांशुर्निपपात वसुंधराम् .. 53 ..
16.20.m: When those women were unable to bear his embryo, / then that cool-rayed one fell from them onto the earth.

16.20.s:
patitaṃ somamālokya brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ..
rathamāropayāmāsa lokānāṃ hitakā myayā .. 54 ..
16.20.d:
पतितं सोममालोक्य ब्रह्मा लोकपितामहः..
रथमारोपयामास लोकानां हितका म्यया .. 54 ..
16.20.m: Seeing Soma fallen, Brahmā, the grandfather of the worlds, / mounted him on a chariot out of a desire for the welfare of the worlds.

16.20.s:
sa tadaiva mayā devi dharmārthaṃ satyasaṃgaraḥ ..
yukto vājisahasreṇa sitena surasuṃdari .. 55 ..
16.20.d:
स तदैव मया देवि धर्मार्थं सत्यसंगरः ..
युक्तो वाजिसहस्रेण सितेन सुरसुंदरि .. 55 ..
16.20.m: At that very time, by me, O goddess, he whose vow is truth was provided, / for the sake of dharma, with a thousand white steeds, O beauty of the gods.

16.20.s:
tasminnipatite devi putretreḥ paramātma ni ..
tuṣṭuvurbrahmaṇaḥ putrā mānasāḥ sapta ye śrutāḥ .. 56 ..
16.20.d:
तस्मिन्निपतिते देवि पुत्रेत्रेः परमात्म नि ..
तुष्टुवुर्ब्रह्मणः पुत्रा मानसाः सप्त ये श्रुताः .. 56 ..
16.20.m: When that supreme soul, the son of Atri, had descended, O goddess, / the seven mind-born sons of Brahmā who are renowned sang his praises,

16.20.s:
tathaivāṃgirasaḥ sarve bhṛgoścaivātmajāstathā ..
ṛgbhistu sāmabhiścaiva tathaivāṃgirasairapi .. .. 57 ..
16.20.d:
तथैवांगिरसः सर्वे भृगोश्चैवात्मजास्तथा ..
ऋग्भिस्तु सामभिश्चैव तथैवांगिरसैरपि .. .. 57 ..
16.20.m: as well as all the descendants of Aṅgiras and the sons of Bhṛgu, / with Ṛg verses, Sāman chants, and verses of the Atharvāṅgirases.

16.20.s:
tasya saṃstūyamānasya tejaḥ somasya bhāsvataḥ ..
āpyāyamānaṃ lokāṃstrīnbhāsayāmāsa sarvaśaḥ .. 58 ..
16.20.d:
तस्य संस्तूयमानस्य तेजः सोमस्य भास्वतः ..
आप्यायमानं लोकांस्त्रीन्भासयामास सर्वशः .. 58 ..
16.20.m: As he was being praised, the radiant splendor of Soma, / swelling fully, illuminated the three worlds on every side.

16.20.s:
sa tena rathamukhyena sāgarāṃtāṃ vasuṃdharām ..
triḥsaptakṛtvotiyaśāścakārābhipradakṣiṇam .. 59 ..
16.20.d:
स तेन रथमुख्येन सागरांतां वसुंधराम् ..
त्रिःसप्तकृत्वोतियशाश्चकाराभिप्रदक्षिणम् .. 59 ..
16.20.m: With that foremost chariot, that one of immense fame / circumambulated the earth bordered by the oceans twenty-one times.

16.20.s:
tasya yaccāpi tattejaḥ pṛthivīmanvapadyata ..
oṣadhyastāḥ samutpannāste jasā'jvalayanpunaḥ .. 7.1.20.60 ..
16.20.d:
तस्य यच्चापि तत्तेजः पृथिवीमन्वपद्यत ..
ओषध्यस्ताः समुत्पन्नास्ते जसाऽज्वलयन्पुनः .. 7.1.20.60 ..
16.20.m: Whatever splendor of his reached the earth, / plants were produced thereby, blazing again with energy.

16.20.s:
tābhirdhinotyayaṃ lokaṃ prajāścaiva caturvidhāḥ ..
oṣadhyaḥ phalapākāṃtāḥ kaṇāḥ saptadaśa smṛtāḥ .. 61 ..
16.20.d:
ताभिर्धिनोत्ययं लोकं प्रजाश्चैव चतुर्विधाः ..
ओषध्यः फलपाकांताः कणाः सप्तदश स्मृताः .. 61 ..
16.20.m:
By them he nourishes this world and the four kinds of living beings.
Annual herbs, which end when their fruit ripens, are traditionally counted as seventeen grains:

16.20.s: vrīhayaśca yavāścaiva godhūmā aṇavastilāḥ .. 62 ..
16.20.d: व्रीहयश्च यवाश्चैव गोधूमा अणवस्तिलाः .. 62 ..
16.20.m: Rice, barley, wheat, small grain, and sesame;

16.20.s:
priyaṃguḥ kovidāraśca koradūṣāḥ satīnakāḥ ..
māṣā mudgā masūrāśca niṣpāvāḥ sakulatthakāḥ .. .. 63 ..
16.20.d:
प्रियंगुः कोविदारश्च कोरदूषाः सतीनकाः ..
माषा मुद्गा मसूराश्च निष्पावाः सकुलत्थकाः .. .. 63 ..
16.20.m:
Italian millet, kovidāra, koradūṣa, and satīnaka peas;
Black gram, mung beans, lentils, kidney beans, along with horse gram;

16.20.s:
āḍhakyaścaṇakāścaiva kaṇāḥ saptadaśa smṛtāḥ ..
ityetā oṣadhīnāṃ ca grāmyāṇāṃ jātayaḥ smṛtāḥ .. 64 ..
16.20.d:
आढक्यश्चणकाश्चैव कणाः सप्तदश स्मृताः ..
इत्येता ओषधीनां च ग्राम्याणां जातयः स्मृताः .. 64 ..
16.20.m:
Pigeon peas and chickpeas: these are recorded as the seventeen grains.
These are traditionally declared to be the cultivated varieties of herbs.

16.20.s:
oṣadhyo yajñiyāścaiva grāmyā raṇyāścaturddaśa ..
vrīhayaśca yavāścaiva godhūmāstvaṇavastilāḥ .. 65 ..
16.20.d:
ओषध्यो यज्ञियाश्चैव ग्राम्या रण्याश्चतुर्द्दश ..
व्रीहयश्च यवाश्चैव गोधूमास्त्वणवस्तिलाः .. 65 ..
16.20.m:
And there are fourteen herbs fit for sacrifice, both cultivated and wild:
Rice, barley, wheat, small grain, and sesame;

16.20.s:
priyaṃguṣaṣṭhā ityete saptamāstu kulatthakāḥ ..
śyāmākāstvatha nīvārā jartilāḥ sagavedhukāḥ .. 66 ..
16.20.d:
प्रियंगुषष्ठा इत्येते सप्तमास्तु कुलत्थकाः ..
श्यामाकास्त्वथ नीवारा जर्तिलाः सगवेधुकाः .. 66 ..
16.20.m:
With Italian millet as the sixth, and horse gram as the seventh;
Then śyāmāka millet, wild rice, wild sesame, along with gavedhuka grass;

16.20.s:
ūruvindā markaṭakāstathā veṇuyavāśca ye ..
grāmyāraṇyāstathā hyetā oṣadhyastu caturdaśa .. 67 ..
16.20.d:
ऊरुविन्दा मर्कटकास्तथा वेणुयवाश्च ये ..
ग्राम्यारण्यास्तथा ह्येता ओषध्यस्तु चतुर्दश .. 67 ..
16.20.m:
Ūruvindā, markaṭaka, and bamboo-seed.
These are indeed the fourteen herbs, both cultivated and wild.

16.20.s:
tṛṇagulmalatā vīrudvallīgucchādi koṭiśaḥ ..
eteṣāmadhipaścandro dhārayatyakhilaṃ jagat .. 68 ..
16.20.d:
तृणगुल्मलता वीरुद्वल्लीगुच्छादि कोटिशः ..
एतेषामधिपश्चन्द्रो धारयत्यखिलं जगत् .. 68 ..
16.20.m:
Grasses, shrubs, creeping plants, medicinal plants, climbing vines, clumps, and others by the tens of millions:
The Moon, the lord of these, sustains the entire world

16.20.s:
jyotsnābhirbhagavānsomo jagato hitakāmyayā ..
tatastasmai dadau rājyaṃ brahmā brahmavidāṃ varaḥ .. 69 ..
16.20.d:
ज्योत्स्नाभिर्भगवान्सोमो जगतो हितकाम्यया ..
ततस्तस्मै ददौ राज्यं ब्रह्मा ब्रह्मविदां वरः .. 69 ..
16.20.m:
With his moonbeams, the lord Soma, out of desire for the welfare of the world.
Then Brahmā, the best of the knowers of Brahman, granted him sovereignty

16.20.s:
bījauṣadhīnāṃ viprāṇāṃ maṃtrāṇāṃ ca varānane ..
so'bhiṣikto mahātejā rājā rājye niśākaraḥ .. 7.1.20.70 ..
16.20.d:
बीजौषधीनां विप्राणां मंत्राणां च वरानने ..
सोऽभिषिक्तो महातेजा राजा राज्ये निशाकरः .. 7.1.20.70 ..
16.20.m:
Over seeds, medicinal herbs, brahmins, and mantras, O fair-faced lady.
Consecrated as king over his realm, the highly radiant maker of the night,

16.20.s:
trīm̐llokānbhāvayāmāsa svabhāsā bhāsvatāṃ varaḥ..
taṃ sinī ca kuhūścaiva dyutiḥpuṣṭiḥ prabhā vasuḥ..71..
16.20.d:
त्रीम्̐ल्लोकान्भावयामास स्वभासा भास्वतां वरः..
तं सिनी च कुहूश्चैव द्युतिःपुष्टिः प्रभा वसुः..71..
16.20.m:
The best of luminous bodies, caused the three worlds to prosper by his own radiance.
To him, Sinīvālī, Kuhū, Dyuti, Puṣṭi, Prabhā, Vasu,

16.20.s:
kīrtirdhṛtiśca lakṣmīśca nava devyaḥ siṣevire..
saptaviṃśatiriṃdostu dākṣāyaṇyo mahāvratāḥ..72..
16.20.d:
कीर्तिर्धृतिश्च लक्ष्मीश्च नव देव्यः सिषेविरे..
सप्तविंशतिरिंदोस्तु दाक्षायण्यो महाव्रताः..72..
16.20.m:
Kīrti, Dhṛti, and Lakṣmī—nine goddesses—rendered service.
Moreover, twenty-seven daughters of Dakṣa of great vows,

16.20.s:
dadau prācetaso dakṣo nakṣatrāṇīti yā viduḥ..
sa tatprāpya mahdrājyaṃ somaḥ somavatāṃ varaḥ .. 73 ..
16.20.d:
ददौ प्राचेतसो दक्षो नक्षत्राणीति या विदुः..
स तत्प्राप्य मह्द्राज्यं सोमः सोमवतां वरः .. 73 ..
16.20.m:
Known as the asterisms, Dakṣa, son of Pracetas, gave to the Moon.
Having obtained that great sovereignty, Soma, the best of the Soma-possessors,

16.20.s:
samājahre rājasūyaṃ sahasraśatadakṣiṇam ..
hiraṇyagarbhaścodgātā brahmā brahmatvameyivān .. 74 ..
16.20.d:
समाजह्रे राजसूयं सहस्रशतदक्षिणम् ..
हिरण्यगर्भश्चोद्गाता ब्रह्मा ब्रह्मत्वमेयिवान् .. 74 ..
16.20.m:
Performed the Rājasūya sacrifice, which has hundreds of thousands of sacrificial gifts.
Hiraṇyagarbha was the Udgātṛ priest, and Brahmā assumed the role of the Brahman priest.

16.20.s:
sadasyastasya bhagavānharirnārāyaṇaḥ prabhuḥ ..
sanatkumārapramukhairādyairbrahmarṣibhirvṛtaḥ .. 75 ..
16.20.d:
सदस्यस्तस्य भगवान्हरिर्नारायणः प्रभुः ..
सनत्कुमारप्रमुखैराद्यैर्ब्रह्मर्षिभिर्वृतः .. 75 ..
16.20.m:
The member of the assembly at his sacrifice was the blessed Lord Hari Nārāyaṇa,
Surrounded by the primordial seer-brahmins headed by Sanatkumāra.

16.20.s:
dakṣiṇāmadadātsomastrīm̐llokāṃstu varānane ..
tebhyo brahmarṣimukhyebhyaḥ sadasyebhyaśca vai śubhe .. .. 76 ..
16.20.d:
दक्षिणामददात्सोमस्त्रीम्̐ल्लोकांस्तु वरानने ..
तेभ्यो ब्रह्मर्षिमुख्येभ्यः सदस्येभ्यश्च वै शुभे .. .. 76 ..
16.20.m:
Soma gave the three worlds as a sacrificial gift, O fair-faced lady,
To those foremost seer-brahmins and members of the sacrificial assembly, O auspicious one.

16.20.s:
prāpyāvabhṛthamavyagraḥ sarvadevarṣipūjitaḥ ..
atirājati rājendro daśadhā bhāvayandiśaḥ .. 77 ..
16.20.d:
प्राप्यावभृथमव्यग्रः सर्वदेवर्षिपूजितः ..
अतिराजति राजेन्द्रो दशधा भावयन्दिशः .. 77 ..
16.20.m:
Having attained the concluding ceremonial bath, untroubled and worshiped by all the divine seers,
The emperor shone forth exceedingly, illuminating the directions tenfold.

16.20.s:
tena tatprāpa duṣprāpyamaiśvaryyamakṛtā tmabhiḥ ..
sa evaṃ varttate candraścātreya iti viśrutaḥ .. 78 ..
iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ saptame prabhāsakhaṇḍe prathame prabhāsakṣetramāhātmye candrotpattivarṇanaṃnāma viṃśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 20 ..
16.20.d:
तेन तत्प्राप दुष्प्राप्यमैश्वर्य्यमकृता त्मभिः ..
स एवं वर्त्तते चन्द्रश्चात्रेय इति विश्रुतः .. 78 ..
इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां सप्तमे प्रभासखण्डे प्रथमे प्रभासक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये चन्द्रोत्पत्तिवर्णनंनाम विंशोऽध्यायः .. 20 ..
16.20.m:
Thereby he attained that sovereign power difficult to obtain by the unrefined.
Thus resides the Moon, renowned as the son of Atri.
Thus ends the twentieth chapter, entitled 'Description of the Origin of the Moon,' in the first [sub-section], the Prabhāsakṣetramāhātmya, of the seventh section, the Prabhāsakhaṇḍa, in the Mahāpurāṇa of eighty-one thousand verses, the glorious Skandapurāṇa.

16.21.s:
.. devyuvāca .. ..
śrutaṃ sarvamaśeṣeṇa candrasyotpatti kāraṇam ..
cihnaṃ yathā'bhavattasya sāṃprataṃ tatprakīrttaya .. 1 ..
16.21.d:
.. देव्युवाच .. ..
श्रुतं सर्वमशेषेण चन्द्रस्योत्पत्ति कारणम् ..
चिह्नं यथाऽभवत्तस्य सांप्रतं तत्प्रकीर्त्तय .. 1 ..
16.21.m:
The Goddess said:
All the cause of the birth of the Moon has been heard in full.
Now declare how that mark of his came to be.

16.21.s:
.. īśvara uvāca .. ..
brahmaṇastu purā devi dakṣo nāma suto'bhavat ..
prajāḥ sṛjeti uddiṣṭaḥ pūrvaṃ dakṣaḥ svayaṃbhuvā .. 2 ..
16.21.d:
.. ईश्वर उवाच .. ..
ब्रह्मणस्तु पुरा देवि दक्षो नाम सुतोऽभवत् ..
प्रजाः सृजेति उद्दिष्टः पूर्वं दक्षः स्वयंभुवा .. 2 ..
16.21.m:
Īśvara said:
Formerly, O goddess, Brahmā had a son named Dakṣa.
Dakṣa was formerly commanded by the Self-born one: 'Create offspring!'

16.21.s:
ṣaṣṭiṃ dakṣo'sṛjatkanyā vairiṇyāṃ vai prajāpatiḥ ..
dadau sa daśa dharmāya kaśyapāya trayodaśa .. 3 ..
16.21.d:
षष्टिं दक्षोऽसृजत्कन्या वैरिण्यां वै प्रजापतिः ..
ददौ स दश धर्माय कश्यपाय त्रयोदश .. 3 ..
16.21.m:
Dakṣa, the lord of creatures, fathered sixty daughters upon Vairiṇī.
He gave ten to Dharma, and thirteen to Kaśyapa;

16.21.s:
sapta viśatiṃ somāya catasro'riṣṭanemine ..
dve caiva bhṛguputrāya dve kṛśāśvāya dhīmate .. 4 ..
16.21.d:
सप्त विशतिं सोमाय चतस्रोऽरिष्टनेमिने ..
द्वे चैव भृगुपुत्राय द्वे कृशाश्वाय धीमते .. 4 ..
16.21.m:
Twenty-seven to the Moon, and four to Ariṣṭanemi;
Two to the son of Bhṛgu, and two to the wise Kṛśāśva;

16.21.s:
dve caivāṃgirase tadvattāsāṃ nāmāni vistarāt ..
śṛṇu tvaṃ devi mātṝṇāṃ prajāvistaramāditaḥ .. 5 ..
16.21.d:
द्वे चैवांगिरसे तद्वत्तासां नामानि विस्तरात् ..
शृणु त्वं देवि मातॄणां प्रजाविस्तरमादितः .. 5 ..
16.21.m:
And likewise two to Aṅgiras. Listen in detail to their names,
O goddess, the mothers, and the expansion of their offspring from the beginning:

16.21.s:
marutvatī vasurjāmī laṃbā bhānurarundhatī ..
saṃkalpā ca muhūrtā ca sādhyā viśvā ca bhāmini .. 6 ..
16.21.d:
मरुत्वती वसुर्जामी लंबा भानुररुन्धती ..
संकल्पा च मुहूर्ता च साध्या विश्वा च भामिनि .. 6 ..
16.21.m:
Marutvatī, Vasu, Jāmī, Lambā, Bhānu, Arundhatī,
Saṃkalpā, Muhūrtā, Sādhyā, and Viśvā, O spirited woman:

16.21.s:
dharma patnyaḥ samākhyātā dakṣaḥ prācetaso dadau ..
aditirditirdanustadvadariṣṭā surasaiva ca .. 7 ..
16.21.d:
धर्म पत्न्यः समाख्याता दक्षः प्राचेतसो ददौ ..
अदितिर्दितिर्दनुस्तद्वदरिष्टा सुरसैव च .. 7 ..
16.21.m:
These are declared to be the wives of Dharma, whom Dakṣa, son of Pracetas, bestowed.
Likewise Aditi, Diti, Danu, Ariṣṭā, and Surasā;

16.21.s:
surabhirvinatā caiva nāmnā krodhavaśā tvilā ..
kadrūstviṣā vasustadvattāsāṃ putrānvadāmi vai .. 8 ..
16.21.d:
सुरभिर्विनता चैव नाम्ना क्रोधवशा त्विला ..
कद्रूस्त्विषा वसुस्तद्वत्तासां पुत्रान्वदामि वै .. 8 ..
16.21.m:
Surabhi, Vinatā, and the one named Krodhavaśā, Ilā,
Kadrū, Tviṣā, and likewise Vasu. Truly, I shall declare their sons:

16.21.s:
viśvedevāstu viśvāyāḥ sādhyā sādhyānajījanat ..
marutvatyāṃ marutvaṃto vasostu vasavastathā .. 9 ...
16.21.d:
विश्वेदेवास्तु विश्वायाः साध्या साध्यानजीजनत् ..
मरुत्वत्यां मरुत्वंतो वसोस्तु वसवस्तथा .. 9 ...
16.21.m:
Viśvā bore the Viśvedevas; Sādhyā gave birth to the Sādhyas;
In Marutvatī were born the Marutvats; and from Vasu, the Vasus;

16.21.s:
bhānostu bhānavastena muhūrttāyāṃ muhūrttakāḥ ..
laṃbāyā ghoṣanāmāno nāgavīthistu jāmijā .. 7.1.21.10 ..
16.21.d:
भानोस्तु भानवस्तेन मुहूर्त्तायां मुहूर्त्तकाः ..
लंबाया घोषनामानो नागवीथिस्तु जामिजा .. 7.1.21.10 ..
16.21.m:
From Bhānu, the Bhānus; through him, in Muhūrtā, the Muhūrtakas;
From Lambā, those named Ghoṣa; and Nāgavīthī was born of Jāmī;

16.21.s:
saṃkalpāyāstu saṃkalpo dharmaputrā daśa smṛtāḥ ..
āpo dhruvaśca somaśca dharaścaivānalo'nilaḥ ..11..
16.21.d:
संकल्पायास्तु संकल्पो धर्मपुत्रा दश स्मृताः ..
आपो ध्रुवश्च सोमश्च धरश्चैवानलोऽनिलः ..11..
16.21.m:
And from Saṃkalpā was born Saṃkalpa: these are known as the ten sons of Dharma.
Āpa, Dhruva, Soma, Dhara, Anala, Anila,

16.21.s:
pratyūṣaśca prabhāsaśca vasavoṣṭau prakīrtitāḥ ..
āpasya putrā vaidaṃḍyaḥ śramaḥ śānto dhvanistathā ... .. 12 ..
16.21.d:
प्रत्यूषश्च प्रभासश्च वसवोष्टौ प्रकीर्तिताः ..
आपस्य पुत्रा वैदंड्यः श्रमः शान्तो ध्वनिस्तथा ... .. 12 ..
16.21.m:
Pratyūṣa, and Prabhāsa are celebrated as the eight Vasus.
The sons of Āpa were Vaidaṇḍya, Śrama, Śānta, and Dhvani;

16.21.s:
dhruvasya putro bhagavānkālo lokaprakālanaḥ ..
somasya bhagavāñcharvo dhruvaśca gṛhabodhanaḥ .. 13 ..
16.21.d:
ध्रुवस्य पुत्रो भगवान्कालो लोकप्रकालनः ..
सोमस्य भगवाञ्छर्वो ध्रुवश्च गृहबोधनः .. 13 ..
16.21.m:
The son of Dhruva was the blessed Kāla, the driver of the world;
The sons of Soma were the blessed Śarva, and Dhruva, who awakens homes;

16.21.s:
hutahavyavahaścaiva dharasya draviṇa smṛtaḥ ..
manojavo'nilasyāsīdavijñātagatistathā .. 14 ..
16.21.d:
हुतहव्यवहश्चैव धरस्य द्रविण स्मृतः ..
मनोजवोऽनिलस्यासीदविज्ञातगतिस्तथा .. 14 ..
16.21.m:
Draviṇa is remembered as the son of Dhara, the bearer of the sacrificial offering;
Manojava and Avijñātagati were the sons of Anila;

16.21.s:
devalo bhagavānyogī pratyūṣasyābhavansutāḥ ..
bṛhaspatestu bhaginī bhuvanā brahmavādinī .. 15 ..
16.21.d:
देवलो भगवान्योगी प्रत्यूषस्याभवन्सुताः ..
बृहस्पतेस्तु भगिनी भुवना ब्रह्मवादिनी .. 15 ..
16.21.m:
The blessed yogi Devala was the son of Pratyūṣa.
The sister of Bṛhaspati was Bhuvanā, who expounded the Veda;

16.21.s:
prabhāsasya tu sā bhāryā vasūnāmaṣṭamasya ca ..
viśvakarmā sutastasya śilpakarttā prajāpatiḥ .. 16 ..
16.21.d:
प्रभासस्य तु सा भार्या वसूनामष्टमस्य च ..
विश्वकर्मा सुतस्तस्य शिल्पकर्त्ता प्रजापतिः .. 16 ..
16.21.m:
She was the wife of Prabhāsa, the eighth of the Vasus.
His son was Viśvakarman, the creator of arts, a lord of creatures.

16.21.s:
tuṣitānāṃ tu sādhyānāṃ nāmānyetāni vacmi te ..
mano'numantā prāṇaśca naro'pānaśca vīryavān .. 17 ..
16.21.d:
तुषितानां तु साध्यानां नामान्येतानि वच्मि ते ..
मनोऽनुमन्ता प्राणश्च नरोऽपानश्च वीर्यवान् .. 17 ..
16.21.m:
I shall tell you these names of the Sādhyas who are the Tuṣitas:
Manas, Anumantṛ, Prāṇa, Nara, and the vigorous Apāna,

16.21.s:
bhaktirbhayo'naghaścaiva haṃso nārāyaṇastathā ..
vibhuścaiva prabhuścaiva sādhyā dvādaśa kīrtitāḥ .. 18 ..
16.21.d:
भक्तिर्भयोऽनघश्चैव हंसो नारायणस्तथा ..
विभुश्चैव प्रभुश्चैव साध्या द्वादश कीर्तिताः .. 18 ..
16.21.m:
Bhakti, Bhaya, Anagha, Haṃsa, and Nārāyaṇa,
Along with Vibhu and Prabhu: twelve Sādhyas are celebrated.

16.21.s:
kaśyapasya pravakṣyāmi santatiṃ varavarṇini ..
aṃśo dhātā bhagastvaṣṭā mitro'tha varuṇo ryamā .. 19 ..
16.21.d:
कश्यपस्य प्रवक्ष्यामि सन्ततिं वरवर्णिनि ..
अंशो धाता भगस्त्वष्टा मित्रोऽथ वरुणो र्यमा .. 19 ..
16.21.m:
I will proclaim the progeny of Kaśyapa, O fair-complexioned lady:
Aṃśa, Dhātṛ, Bhaga, Tvaṣṭṛ, Mitra, then Varuṇa, Aryaman,

16.21.s:
vivasvānsavitā pūṣā hyaṃśumānviṣṇureva ca ..
ete sahasrakiraṇā ādityā dvādaśa smṛtāḥ .. 7.1.21.20 ..
16.21.d:
विवस्वान्सविता पूषा ह्यंशुमान्विष्णुरेव च ..
एते सहस्रकिरणा आदित्या द्वादश स्मृताः .. 7.1.21.20 ..
16.21.m:
Vivasvat, Savitṛ, Pūṣan, Aṃśumat, and Viṣṇu:
These thousand-rayed ones are remembered as the twelve Ādityas.

16.21.s:
ajaikapādahirbudhnyo virūpākṣo'tha raivataḥ ..
haraśca bahurūpaśca tryaṃbakaśca sureśvaraḥ .. 21 ..
16.21.d:
अजैकपादहिर्बुध्न्यो विरूपाक्षोऽथ रैवतः ..
हरश्च बहुरूपश्च त्र्यंबकश्च सुरेश्वरः .. 21 ..
16.21.m:
Ajaikapād, Ahirbudhnya, Virūpākṣa, then Raivata,
Hara, Bahurūpa, Tryambaka, Sureśvara,

16.21.s:
sāvitraśca jayantaśca pinākī cāparājitaḥ ..
ete rudrāḥ samākhyātā ekādaśa gaṇeśvarāḥ .. 22 ..
16.21.d:
सावित्रश्च जयन्तश्च पिनाकी चापराजितः ..
एते रुद्राः समाख्याता एकादश गणेश्वराः .. 22 ..
16.21.m:
Sāvitra, Jayanta, Pinākin, and Aparājita:
These are declared to be the Rudras, the eleven lords of the gaṇas.

16.21.s:
ditiḥ putradvayaṃ lebhe kaśyapādbalagarvitam ..
hiraṇyakaśipuṃ śreṣṭhaṃ hiraṇyākṣaṃ tathānujam .. 23 ..
16.21.d:
दितिः पुत्रद्वयं लेभे कश्यपाद्बलगर्वितम् ..
हिरण्यकशिपुं श्रेष्ठं हिरण्याक्षं तथानुजम् .. 23 ..
16.21.m:
Diti obtained two sons from Kaśyapa, proud of their strength:
Hiraṇyakaśipu, the eldest, and likewise his younger brother Hiraṇyākṣa.

16.21.s: hiraṇyakaśipordaityaiḥ ślokogītaḥ purātanaiḥ ..24..
16.21.d: हिरण्यकशिपोर्दैत्यैः श्लोकोगीतः पुरातनैः ..24..
16.21.m: A verse concerning Hiraṇyakaśipu was sung by the ancient Daityas:

16.21.s:
rājā hiraṇyakaśipuryāṃyāmāśāṃ nirīkṣate ..
tasyāṃ tasyāṃ diśi surā namaścakrurmaharṣibhiḥ ..
hiraṇyakaśipoḥ putrāścatvāraḥ sumahābalāḥ .. 25 ..
16.21.d:
राजा हिरण्यकशिपुर्यांयामाशां निरीक्षते ..
तस्यां तस्यां दिशि सुरा नमश्चक्रुर्महर्षिभिः ..
हिरण्यकशिपोः पुत्राश्चत्वारः सुमहाबलाः .. 25 ..
16.21.m:
'Whichever direction King Hiraṇyakaśipu looks upon,
In that very direction the gods together with the great seers bowed down.'
The sons of Hiraṇyakaśipu were four, of very great might.

16.21.s:
prahlādaḥ pūrvajasteṣāmanuhrādastataḥ paraḥ ..
hrādaścaiva hradaścaiva putrāścaite prakīrtitāḥ .. 26 ..
16.21.d:
प्रह्लादः पूर्वजस्तेषामनुह्रादस्ततः परः ..
ह्रादश्चैव ह्रदश्चैव पुत्राश्चैते प्रकीर्तिताः .. 26 ..
16.21.m: Prahlāda was the eldest of them; Anuhrāda was after him; / and Hrāda and Hrada are proclaimed to be their sons.

16.21.s:
ubhau sundopasundau tu hradaputrau babhūvatuḥ ..
hrādasya putrastveko'bhūnmūka ityabhiviśrutaḥ .. 27 ..
16.21.d:
उभौ सुन्दोपसुन्दौ तु ह्रदपुत्रौ बभूवतुः ..
ह्रादस्य पुत्रस्त्वेकोऽभून्मूक इत्यभिविश्रुतः .. 27 ..
16.21.m: Both Sunda and Upasunda were the sons of Hrada. / Hrāda had one son, celebrated as Mūka.

16.21.s:
mārīcaḥ suṃdaputrastu tāḍakāyāmajāyata ..
daṇḍake nihataḥ so'yaṃ rāghaveṇa valīyasā .. 28 ..
16.21.d:
मारीचः सुंदपुत्रस्तु ताडकायामजायत ..
दण्डके निहतः सोऽयं राघवेण वलीयसा .. 28 ..
16.21.m: Mārīca, the son of Sunda, was born of Tāḍakā; / he was slain in the Daṇḍaka forest by the mighty descendant of Raghu.

16.21.s:
mūko vinihataścāpi kairāte sabyasācinā ..
saṃhrādasya tu daityasya nivātakavacāḥ kule .. 29 ..
16.21.d:
मूको विनिहतश्चापि कैराते सब्यसाचिना ..
संह्रादस्य तु दैत्यस्य निवातकवचाः कुले .. 29 ..
16.21.m: Mūka too was slain by Savyasācin in Kirāta guise. / In the lineage of the daitya Saṃhrāda were the Nivātakavacas:

16.21.s:
tisraḥ koṭyastu vikhyātā nihatāḥ savyasācinā..
gaveṣṭhī kālanemiśca jaṃbho valkala eva ca .. 7.1.21.30 ..
16.21.d:
तिस्रः कोट्यस्तु विख्याता निहताः सव्यसाचिना..
गवेष्ठी कालनेमिश्च जंभो वल्कल एव च .. 7.1.21.30 ..
16.21.m: thirty million renowned ones were slain by Savyasācin. / Gaveṣṭhin, Kālanemi, Jambha, and Valkala,

16.21.s:
jṛṃbhaḥ ṣaṣṭhonujasteṣāṃ smṛtāḥ prahrādasūnavaḥ ..
śuṃbhaścaiva niśuṃbhaśca gaveṣṭhinaḥ sutau smṛtau ..31..
16.21.d:
जृंभः षष्ठोनुजस्तेषां स्मृताः प्रह्रादसूनवः ..
शुंभश्चैव निशुंभश्च गवेष्ठिनः सुतौ स्मृतौ ..31..
16.21.m: and Jṛmbha, their sixth and youngest, are remembered as the sons of Prahrāda. / Śumbha and Niśumbha are recorded as the two sons of Gaveṣṭhin.

16.21.s:
dhanukaścāsilomā ca śuṃbhaputrau prakīrtitau ..
virocanasya putrastu balirekaḥ pratāpavān .. 32 ..
16.21.d:
धनुकश्चासिलोमा च शुंभपुत्रौ प्रकीर्तितौ ..
विरोचनस्य पुत्रस्तु बलिरेकः प्रतापवान् .. 32 ..
16.21.m: Dhanuka and Asiloman are declared to be the two sons of Śumbha. / Virocana, however, had one glorious son, Bali.

16.21.s:
hiraṇyākṣasutāḥ paṃca vikrāṃtāḥ sumahābalāḥ ..
andhakaḥ śakuniścaiva kālanābhastathaiva ca .. 33 ..
16.21.d:
हिरण्याक्षसुताः पंच विक्रांताः सुमहाबलाः ..
अन्धकः शकुनिश्चैव कालनाभस्तथैव च .. 33 ..
16.21.m: Hiraṇyākṣa had five valiant and exceedingly powerful sons: / Andhaka, Śakuni, and Kālanābha,

16.21.s:
mahānābhaśca vikrāṃto bhūtasaṃtāpanastathā ..
śataṃ śatasahasrāṇi nihatāstārakāmaye .. 34 ..
16.21.d:
महानाभश्च विक्रांतो भूतसंतापनस्तथा ..
शतं शतसहस्राणि निहतास्तारकामये .. 34 ..
16.21.m: as well as the valiant Mahānābha and Bhūtasaṃtāpana. / One hundred hundred-thousands of them were slain in the Tārakāmaya war.

16.21.s:
iti saṃkṣapataḥ proktā kaśyapānvayasaṃtatiḥ ..
yayā vyāptaṃ jagatsarvaṃ sadevāsuramānuṣam .. 35 ..
16.21.d:
इति संक्षपतः प्रोक्ता कश्यपान्वयसंततिः ..
यया व्याप्तं जगत्सर्वं सदेवासुरमानुषम् .. 35 ..
16.21.m: Thus the lineage of the descendants of Kaśyapa has been stated in brief, / by which the entire world, containing gods, asuras, and mortals, was pervaded.

16.21.s:
atha yāḥ kanyakā dattāḥ saptaviṃśatiriṃdave ..
tāsāṃ madhye mahādevi priyā tasya ca rohiṇī .. 36 ..
16.21.d:
अथ याः कन्यका दत्ताः सप्तविंशतिरिंदवे ..
तासां मध्ये महादेवि प्रिया तस्य च रोहिणी .. 36 ..
16.21.m: Now, of the twenty-seven maidens given to the Moon, / among them, O great goddess, Rohiṇī was his beloved.

16.21.s:
atha nakṣatranāthasya tāsāṃ madhyetivallabhā ..
babhūva rohiṇī devī prāṇebhyo'pi garīyasī .. 37 ..
16.21.d:
अथ नक्षत्रनाथस्य तासां मध्येतिवल्लभा ..
बभूव रोहिणी देवी प्राणेभ्योऽपि गरीयसी .. 37 ..
16.21.m: Then, among them, the goddess Rohiṇī became exceedingly dear / to the lord of the asterisms, dearer even than his own breaths of life.

16.21.s:
sarvāstāḥ saṃparityajya rohiṇyā sahito rahaḥ ..
reme kāmaparītātmā vaneṣūpavaneṣu ca ..
ramaṇīyeṣu deśeṣu kandareṣu guhāsu ca .. 38 ..
16.21.d:
सर्वास्ताः संपरित्यज्य रोहिण्या सहितो रहः ..
रेमे कामपरीतात्मा वनेषूपवनेषु च ..
रमणीयेषु देशेषु कन्दरेषु गुहासु च .. 38 ..
16.21.m: Abandoning all of them, he sported in secret with Rohiṇī, / his mind overwhelmed by desire, in forests and groves, / in delightful regions, in ravines, and in caves.

16.21.s:
atha tā duḥkhasaṃpannāḥ patnyaḥ śeṣā yaśasvini ..
jagmuśca śaraṇaṃ dakṣaṃ vacanaṃ cedamabruvan .. 39 ..
16.21.d:
अथ ता दुःखसंपन्नाः पत्न्यः शेषा यशस्विनि ..
जग्मुश्च शरणं दक्षं वचनं चेदमब्रुवन् .. 39 ..
16.21.m: Then the remaining wives, filled with grief, O glorious one, / went to Dakṣa for refuge and spoke these words:

16.21.s:
somaḥ sarvā tikramya rohiṇyā saha modate ..
saṃvatsarasahasraṃ tu krīḍamāno yathāsukham .. 7.1.21.40 ..
16.21.d:
सोमः सर्वा तिक्रम्य रोहिण्या सह मोदते ..
संवत्सरसहस्रं तु क्रीडमानो यथासुखम् .. 7.1.21.40 ..
16.21.m: “Soma, having neglected all of us, delights with Rohiṇī, / sporting as he pleases for a thousand years.

16.21.s:
avaśiṣṭāstu ṣaḍviṃśanmalinā vigataśriyaḥ ..
pāṇigrahaṇamārabhya rohiṇyā saha caṃdramāḥ .. 41 ..
16.21.d:
अवशिष्टास्तु षड्विंशन्मलिना विगतश्रियः ..
पाणिग्रहणमारभ्य रोहिण्या सह चंद्रमाः .. 41 ..
16.21.m: The remaining twenty-six of us have become wretched and stripped of splendor. / Ever since marriage, the Moon, together with Rohiṇī,

16.21.s:
saṃvatsarasahasraṃ tu jānātyekāṃ sa śarvarīm ..
parityaktā vayaṃ tāta śaśinā doṣavarjitāḥ .. 42 ..
16.21.d:
संवत्सरसहस्रं तु जानात्येकां स शर्वरीम् ..
परित्यक्ता वयं तात शशिना दोषवर्जिताः .. 42 ..
16.21.m: regards a thousand years as merely a single night. / We, father, although free of fault, have been abandoned by the Moon.

16.21.s:
sa reme saha rohiṇyā asmākamasukhapradaḥ ..
asmākaṃ duḥkhadagdhānāṃ śreyo'to maraṇaṃ bhavet .. 43 ..
16.21.d:
स रेमे सह रोहिण्या अस्माकमसुखप्रदः ..
अस्माकं दुःखदग्धानां श्रेयोऽतो मरणं भवेत् .. 43 ..
16.21.m: He delights with Rohiṇī, bringing misery upon us. / For us, consumed by sorrow, death would be better than this.”

16.21.s:
tāsāṃ tadvacanaṃ śrutvā duḥkhārtānāṃ prajāpatiḥ ..
brahmatejaḥ samāyuktaḥ putrīsnehena karṣitaḥ ..
jagāma yatra ṛkṣeśo vacanaṃ cedamabravīt .. 44 ..
16.21.d:
तासां तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा दुःखार्तानां प्रजापतिः ..
ब्रह्मतेजः समायुक्तः पुत्रीस्नेहेन कर्षितः ..
जगाम यत्र ऋक्षेशो वचनं चेदमब्रवीत् .. 44 ..
16.21.m: Hearing those words of theirs, tormented by distress, the Prajāpati, / endowed with brāhmaṇa-splendor and distressed by affection for his daughters, / went to where the lord of constellations was, and spoke these words:

16.21.s:
samaṃ varttasva kanyāsu māmakāsu niśākara ..
anyathā doṣabhāgī tvaṃ bhaviṣyasi na saṃśayaḥ .. 45 ..
16.21.d:
समं वर्त्तस्व कन्यासु मामकासु निशाकर ..
अन्यथा दोषभागी त्वं भविष्यसि न संशयः .. 45 ..
16.21.m: “Behave equally toward my daughters, O maker of the night. / Otherwise, you will incur fault—of this there is no doubt.”

16.21.s:
tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā lajjayāvanataḥ sthitaḥ ..
bāḍhamityeva ṛkṣeṃdro dakṣasya purato'bravīt .. 46 ..
16.21.d:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा लज्जयावनतः स्थितः ..
बाढमित्येव ऋक्षेंद्रो दक्षस्य पुरतोऽब्रवीत् .. 46 ..
16.21.m: Hearing his words, standing bowed with shame, / the lord of the stars said to Dakṣa, “Very well.”

16.21.s:
adyaprabhṛti viprarṣe samaṃ varttayitāsmyaham..
putrībhistava satyaṃ vai śape'haṃ śapathena te .. 47 ..
16.21.d:
अद्यप्रभृति विप्रर्षे समं वर्त्तयितास्म्यहम्..
पुत्रीभिस्तव सत्यं वै शपेऽहं शपथेन ते .. 47 ..
16.21.m: “From this day forward, O brahmin-seer, I shall behave equally / toward your daughters; truly, I swear to you by an oath.”

16.21.s:
evaṃ pratijñāsaṃyukte niśānāthe tadāṃbike ..
sarvā rūpeṇa saṃyuktāstasya kanyā niveditāḥ .. 48 ..
16.21.d:
एवं प्रतिज्ञासंयुक्ते निशानाथे तदांबिके ..
सर्वा रूपेण संयुक्तास्तस्य कन्या निवेदिताः .. 48 ..
16.21.m: When the lord of the night had thus bound himself by a vow, O Ambikā, / all the daughters, endowed with beauty, were committed to him.

16.21.s:
dakṣaḥ svabhavanaṃ gatvā nirvṛtiṃ paramāṃ gataḥ ..
candro'pi pūrvavaddevi rohiṇyāṃ nirato'bhavat .. 49 ..
16.21.d:
दक्षः स्वभवनं गत्वा निर्वृतिं परमां गतः ..
चन्द्रोऽपि पूर्ववद्देवि रोहिण्यां निरतोऽभवत् .. 49 ..
16.21.m: Dakṣa, having gone to his own abode, attained supreme relief. / The Moon, however, O goddess, became devoted to Rohiṇī just as before.

16.21.s:
saṃparityajya tāḥ sarvāḥ kāmopahatamānasaḥ ..
atha bhūyastu tāḥ sarvā dakṣaṃ vacanamabruvan .. 7.1.21.50 ..
16.21.d:
संपरित्यज्य ताः सर्वाः कामोपहतमानसः ..
अथ भूयस्तु ताः सर्वा दक्षं वचनमब्रुवन् .. 7.1.21.50 ..
16.21.m: Abandoning all of them, his mind stricken by passion, / then again all of them spoke these words to Dakṣa:

16.21.s:
malināstāḥ kṛśāṃgyaśca dīnāḥ sarvā vicetasaḥ ..
tato dṛṣṭvā tathārūpaṃ dakṣo mohamupāgataḥ .. 51 ..
16.21.d:
मलिनास्ताः कृशांग्यश्च दीनाः सर्वा विचेतसः ..
ततो दृष्ट्वा तथारूपं दक्षो मोहमुपागतः .. 51 ..
16.21.m: They were unclean, their limbs emaciated, all miserable and distraught. / Thereupon, seeing them in such a state, Dakṣa fell into bewilderment.

16.21.s:
labdhasaṃjñaḥ punaḥ so'pi krodhodbhūtatanūruhaḥ ..
uvāca sarvāḥ svāḥ putrīḥ kimitthaṃ malināṃbarāḥ ..
kimidaṃ niṣprabhāḥ sarvāḥ kathayadhvaṃ mamānaghāḥ .. 52 ..
16.21.d:
लब्धसंज्ञः पुनः सोऽपि क्रोधोद्भूततनूरुहः ..
उवाच सर्वाः स्वाः पुत्रीः किमित्थं मलिनांबराः ..
किमिदं निष्प्रभाः सर्वाः कथयध्वं ममानघाः .. 52 ..
16.21.m: Regaining consciousness, his body hair bristling with rage, / he spoke to all his daughters: “Why are your garments soiled like this? / Why are you all devoid of luster? Tell me, blameless ones!

16.21.s:
asurānsānugāṃścaiva ye cānye surasattamāḥ ..
adya śāpahatānputryaḥ kariṣyāmi na saṃśayaḥ .. 53 ..
16.21.d:
असुरान्सानुगांश्चैव ये चान्ये सुरसत्तमाः ..
अद्य शापहतान्पुत्र्यः करिष्यामि न संशयः .. 53 ..
16.21.m: Whether the asuras with their followers, or whoever else among the best of the gods [it may be], / I shall today make them struck down by a curse, O daughters—of this there is no doubt.”

16.21.s: evamuktāstu dakṣeṇa sarvāstāḥ samudairayan .. 54 ..
16.21.d: एवमुक्तास्तु दक्षेण सर्वास्ताः समुदैरयन् .. 54 ..
16.21.m: Being thus addressed by Dakṣa, all of them declared:

16.21.s:
na cāsmākaṃ niśānātha ṛtumātramapi prabho ..
prayacchati punastena yuṣmatpārśvaṃ samāgatāḥ .. 55 ..
16.21.d:
न चास्माकं निशानाथ ऋतुमात्रमपि प्रभो ..
प्रयच्छति पुनस्तेन युष्मत्पार्श्वं समागताः .. 55 ..
16.21.m: “The lord of the night does not grant us even the time suitable for conception, O lord! / Therefore we have come again to your presence.

16.21.s:
anādṛtya tu te vākyaṃ rohiṇyāṃ nirato rahaḥ ..
reme kāmaparītātmā asmākaṃ śokavarddhanaḥ .. 56 ..
16.21.d:
अनादृत्य तु ते वाक्यं रोहिण्यां निरतो रहः ..
रेमे कामपरीतात्मा अस्माकं शोकवर्द्धनः .. 56 ..
16.21.m: Disregarding your command, devoted to Rohiṇī in secret, / he has sported, his mind overwhelmed by desire, multiplying our grief.”

16.21.s:
tāsāṃ tadvacanaṃ śrutvā dakṣaḥ kopamupāgataḥ ..
gatvā caṃdraṃ mahādevi śaśāpa pramukhe sthitam.. 57 ..
16.21.d:
तासां तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा दक्षः कोपमुपागतः ..
गत्वा चंद्रं महादेवि शशाप प्रमुखे स्थितम्.. 57 ..
16.21.m: Hearing their words, Dakṣa was filled with wrath. / Going to the Moon standing before him, O great goddess, he cursed him:

16.21.s:
anādṛtya hi me vākyaṃ yasmāttvaṃ rohiṇīrataḥ ..
saṃtyajya putrīścāsmākaṃ śeṣā doṣeṇa varjitāḥ ..
tasmādyakṣmā śarīraṃ te grasiṣyati na saṃśayaḥ.. .. 58 ..
16.21.d:
अनादृत्य हि मे वाक्यं यस्मात्त्वं रोहिणीरतः ..
संत्यज्य पुत्रीश्चास्माकं शेषा दोषेण वर्जिताः ..
तस्माद्यक्ष्मा शरीरं ते ग्रसिष्यति न संशयः.. .. 58 ..
16.21.m: “Since, disregarding my command, you remain devoted to Rohiṇī, / having abandoned the rest of my daughters who are free from fault, / therefore consumption shall seize your body, without a doubt.”

16.21.s:
etasminneva kāle tu yakṣmā parvataputrike ..
dakṣeṇa tu samādiṣṭastasya kāyaṃ samāviśat .. 59 ..
16.21.d:
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु यक्ष्मा पर्वतपुत्रिके ..
दक्षेण तु समादिष्टस्तस्य कायं समाविशत् .. 59 ..
16.21.m: At that very moment, O daughter of the mountain, / consumption, commanded by Dakṣa, entered his body.

16.21.s: yakṣmaṇā grastakāyo'sau kṣayaṃ yāti dinedine .. 7.1.21.60 ..
16.21.d: यक्ष्मणा ग्रस्तकायोऽसौ क्षयं याति दिनेदिने .. 7.1.21.60 ..
16.21.m: His body seized by consumption, he wasted away day by day.

16.21.s:
evaṃ somastu dakṣeṇa kṛtaśāpo gataprabhaḥ ..
papāta vasudhāṃ devi niśceṣṭo rohiṇīyutaḥ .. 61 ..
16.21.d:
एवं सोमस्तु दक्षेण कृतशापो गतप्रभः ..
पपात वसुधां देवि निश्चेष्टो रोहिणीयुतः .. 61 ..
16.21.m: Thus cursed by Dakṣa, the Moon, stripped of his luster, / fell to the earth motionless, O goddess, along with Rohiṇī.

16.21.s: labdhvasaṃjño muhūrtena rohiṇīvākya mabravīt .62.
16.21.d: लब्ध्वसंज्ञो मुहूर्तेन रोहिणीवाक्य मब्रवीत् .62.
16.21.m: Having regained consciousness after a moment, he spoke these words to Rohiṇī:

16.21.s:
devi kāryaṃ kimadhunā tvatpitrā śāpito hyaham..
kṣayakuṣṭhena saṃyuktaḥ kiṃ karomyadhunā priye..63..
16.21.d:
देवि कार्यं किमधुना त्वत्पित्रा शापितो ह्यहम्..
क्षयकुष्ठेन संयुक्तः किं करोम्यधुना प्रिये..63..
16.21.m: “O goddess, what is to be done now? Indeed, I have been cursed by your father! / Afflicted with consumptive disease, what shall I do now, beloved?”

16.21.s:
evamuktā rohiṇī tu bāṣpavyākulalocanā..
dakṣaśāpahataṃ dṛṣṭvā somaṃ vacanamabravīt..64..
16.21.d:
एवमुक्ता रोहिणी तु बाष्पव्याकुललोचना..
दक्षशापहतं दृष्ट्वा सोमं वचनमब्रवीत्..64..
16.21.m: Thus addressed, Rohiṇī, her eyes filled with tears, / seeing Soma stricken by Dakṣa's curse, spoke these words:

16.21.s:
yena śāpastu te dattastameva śaraṇaṃ vraja..
sa te śāpābhibhūtasya nūnaṃ śreyo vidhāsyati.. 65..
16.21.d:
येन शापस्तु ते दत्तस्तमेव शरणं व्रज..
स ते शापाभिभूतस्य नूनं श्रेयो विधास्यति.. 65..
16.21.m: “Go for refuge to that very one by whom the curse was given to you. / He will surely bring about good for you who are overwhelmed by the curse.

16.21.s: lapsyase tatprasādāttvaṃ prabhāṃ pūrvocitāṃ śubhām.. 66..
16.21.d: लप्स्यसे तत्प्रसादात्त्वं प्रभां पूर्वोचितां शुभाम्.. 66..
16.21.m: By his grace, you will regain your former auspicious splendor.”

16.21.s:
rohiṇyā vacanaṃ śrutvā gato dakṣasamīpataḥ ..
caṃdraḥ provāca vinayādvāṣpa vyākulalocanaḥ .. 67 ..
16.21.d:
रोहिण्या वचनं श्रुत्वा गतो दक्षसमीपतः ..
चंद्रः प्रोवाच विनयाद्वाष्प व्याकुललोचनः .. 67 ..
16.21.m: Hearing Rohiṇī's words, the Moon went near Dakṣa / and spoke with humility, his eyes filled with tears:

16.21.s:
kuruṣvānugrahaṃ dakṣa prasannenāṃtarātmanā ..
kopaṃ tyaja maharṣe tvaṃ mamopari dayāṃ kuru .1 68 ..
16.21.d:
कुरुष्वानुग्रहं दक्ष प्रसन्नेनांतरात्मना ..
कोपं त्यज महर्षे त्वं ममोपरि दयां कुरु .1 68 ..
16.21.m: “Show favor, O Dakṣa, with a gracious inner heart. / Renounce your anger, O great seer, and have pity upon me!

16.21.s:
tvayā krodhaparītena kāraṇe vāpyakāraṇe ..
anukaṃpāṃ ca me kṛtvā kāryaṃ śāpasya mokṣaṇam.. 69 ..
16.21.d:
त्वया क्रोधपरीतेन कारणे वाप्यकारणे ..
अनुकंपां च मे कृत्वा कार्यं शापस्य मोक्षणम्.. 69 ..
16.21.m: Whether with cause or without cause [it was done] by you overwhelmed with wrath, / have compassion on me and effect the release of the curse!

16.21.s:
viditaṃ tu mahābhāga śaptohaṃ yena karmaṇā ..
kuruṣvānugrahaṃ dakṣa mama dīnasya yācataḥ .. 7.1.21.70 ..
16.21.d:
विदितं तु महाभाग शप्तोहं येन कर्मणा ..
कुरुष्वानुग्रहं दक्ष मम दीनस्य याचतः .. 7.1.21.70 ..
16.21.m: It is known, O noble one, by what deed I was cursed; / grant favor, O Dakṣa, to me who am miserable and begging!”

16.21.s:
evaṃ vilapamānasya somasya tu mahātmanaḥ ..
anugrahe matiṃ kṛtvā idaṃ vacanamabravīt ..71..
16.21.d:
एवं विलपमानस्य सोमस्य तु महात्मनः ..
अनुग्रहे मतिं कृत्वा इदं वचनमब्रवीत् ..71..
16.21.m: As the great-souled Soma was thus lamenting, / making up his mind to grant grace, [Dakṣa] spoke these words:

16.21.s:
.. dakṣa uvāca .. ..
mayā śāpahataḥ soma trātuṃ śakyo na daivataiḥ..
yadyadbravīmyahaṃ soma tattatheti na saṃśayaḥ .. 72 ..
16.21.d:
.. दक्ष उवाच .. ..
मया शापहतः सोम त्रातुं शक्यो न दैवतैः..
यद्यद्ब्रवीम्यहं सोम तत्तथेति न संशयः .. 72 ..
16.21.m: Dakṣa said: / Struck down by my curse, O Soma, you cannot be protected by the gods. / Whatever I say, O Soma, is indeed so; there is no doubt.

16.21.s:
āyuḥ karma ca vittaṃ ca vidyā nidhanameva ca ..
pūrvasṛṣṭāni yānyeva saṃbhavaṃti hi tāni vai .. 73 ..
16.21.d:
आयुः कर्म च वित्तं च विद्या निधनमेव च ..
पूर्वसृष्टानि यान्येव संभवंति हि तानि वै .. 73 ..
16.21.m: Lifespan, actions, wealth, learning, and death itself— / whatever has been created beforehand, those indeed come to pass.

16.21.s:
asurāśca surāścaiva ye cānye yakṣarākṣasāḥ ..
sarvepi śaktā na trātuṃ varjayitvā maheśvaram ..74..
16.21.d:
असुराश्च सुराश्चैव ये चान्ये यक्षराक्षसाः ..
सर्वेपि शक्ता न त्रातुं वर्जयित्वा महेश्वरम् ..74..
16.21.m: Asuras and gods, and whatever other yakṣas and rākṣasas there are, / are all incapable of protecting [you], except Maheśvara.

16.21.s:
eṣāṃ śāpo mayā datto'nugrahīṣya ti śaṃkaraḥ..
nānyastrātuṃ bhavecchakto vinā paśupatiṃ bhavam ..
tattvaṃ śīghrataraṃ gaccha samārādhaya śaṃkara .. 75 ..
16.21.d:
एषां शापो मया दत्तोऽनुग्रहीष्य ति शंकरः..
नान्यस्त्रातुं भवेच्छक्तो विना पशुपतिं भवम् ..
तत्त्वं शीघ्रतरं गच्छ समाराधय शंकर .. 75 ..
16.21.m: A curse was given to these by me, [and] Śaṃkara will bestow his grace. / No other could be able to protect [you], except Bhava, Paśupati. / Therefore go very quickly [and] worship Śaṃkara.

16.21.s:
na śakto'nyaḥ punaścaṃdraḥ kartuṃ tvāṃ nirmalaṃ punaḥ..
varjayitvā mahādevaṃ śitikaṃṭhamumāpatim ..76..
16.21.d:
न शक्तोऽन्यः पुनश्चंद्रः कर्तुं त्वां निर्मलं पुनः..
वर्जयित्वा महादेवं शितिकंठमुमापतिम् ..76..
16.21.m: No one else is able, O Moon, to make you spotless again, / except Mahādeva, the blue-throated lord of Umā.

16.21.s:
dakṣasya ca vacaḥ śrutvā kṛtāṃjalipuṭaḥ sthitaḥ..
pratyuvāca tadā somaḥ prahaṣṭenāṃtarātmanā..77..
16.21.d:
दक्षस्य च वचः श्रुत्वा कृतांजलिपुटः स्थितः..
प्रत्युवाच तदा सोमः प्रहष्टेनांतरात्मना..77..
16.21.m: Having heard Dakṣa's speech, standing with hands folded in reverence, / Soma then replied with a heart filled with joy:

16.21.s:
bhagavanyadi tuṣṭosi mama bhaktasya suvrata ..
anugrahe kṛtā buddhistadācakṣva kutaḥ śivaḥ .. 78 ..
16.21.d:
भगवन्यदि तुष्टोसि मम भक्तस्य सुव्रत ..
अनुग्रहे कृता बुद्धिस्तदाचक्ष्व कुतः शिवः .. 78 ..
16.21.m: O Lord of good vows, if you are pleased with me, your devotee, / [and] your mind is made up to grant grace, then tell [me]: where is Śiva?

16.21.s:
kasminsthāne mayā dakṣa draṣṭavyo'sau maheśvaraḥ ..
tatsthānāni cariṣyāmi yāni tāni vadasva me .. 79 ..
16.21.d:
कस्मिन्स्थाने मया दक्ष द्रष्टव्योऽसौ महेश्वरः ..
तत्स्थानानि चरिष्यामि यानि तानि वदस्व मे .. 79 ..
16.21.m: In what place, O Dakṣa, am I to behold that Maheśvara? / I will go to those places; speak to me of whichever they are.

16.21.s:
.. dakṣa uvāca .. ..
śṛṇu soma prayatnena śrutvā caivāvadhāraya ..
vāruṇīṃ diśamāśritya sāgarānūpasannidhau .. 7.1.21.80 ..
16.21.d:
.. दक्ष उवाच .. ..
शृणु सोम प्रयत्नेन श्रुत्वा चैवावधारय ..
वारुणीं दिशमाश्रित्य सागरानूपसन्निधौ .. 7.1.21.80 ..
16.21.m: Dakṣa said: / Listen attentively, O Soma, and having listened, keep it in mind: / having resorted to the western direction, near the shore of the ocean,

16.21.s:
kṛtasmarasyāparato dhanvaṃtaraśatatraye ..
liṃgaṃ mahāprabhāvaṃ ca svayaṃbhūtaṃ vyavasthitam .. 81 ..
16.21.d:
कृतस्मरस्यापरतो धन्वंतरशतत्रये ..
लिंगं महाप्रभावं च स्वयंभूतं व्यवस्थितम् .. 81 ..
16.21.m: three hundred bow-lengths to the west of Kṛtasmara, / there stands a self-manifest liṅga of great power,

16.21.s:
sūryyabiṃbasamaprakhyaṃ sarpa mekhalamaṃḍitam..
kukkuṭāṃḍakamānaṃ tadbhūmimadhye vyavasthitam .. 82 ..
16.21.d:
सूर्य्यबिंबसमप्रख्यं सर्प मेखलमंडितम्..
कुक्कुटांडकमानं तद्भूमिमध्ये व्यवस्थितम् .. 82 ..
16.21.m: resembling the disk of the sun, adorned with a girdle of serpents, / the size of a hen's egg, situated in the midst of the earth.

16.21.s:
sparśaliṃgaṃ hi tadviddhi tadbhaktyā jñāsyate bhavān ..
tatra saṃnihito devaḥ śaṃkaraḥ parameśvaraḥ .. 83 ..
16.21.d:
स्पर्शलिंगं हि तद्विद्धि तद्भक्त्या ज्ञास्यते भवान् ..
तत्र संनिहितो देवः शंकरः परमेश्वरः .. 83 ..
16.21.m: Know it indeed as the Sparśaliṅga; you will recognize it through devotion to it. / Present there is the god Śaṃkara, Parameśvara.

16.21.s:
gaccha tvaṃ tapasogreṇa ārādhaya sureśvaram .. 94 ..
praśasya devadeveśamātmānaṃ nirmalaṃ kuru ..
yasyāśu varadānena prāpsyase rūpamuttamam .. 85 ..
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasyāsaṃhitāyāṃ saptame prabhāsakhaṇḍe prathame prabhāsakṣetramāhātmye someśvarotpattiprasaṃge dakṣeṇa svaśāpajanyayakṣmarogārttasya caṃdrasya yakṣmakuṣṭharoganivṛttaye śivārādhanopadeśavarṇanaṃnāmaikaviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 21 ..
16.21.d:
गच्छ त्वं तपसोग्रेण आराधय सुरेश्वरम् .. 94 ..
प्रशस्य देवदेवेशमात्मानं निर्मलं कुरु ..
यस्याशु वरदानेन प्राप्स्यसे रूपमुत्तमम् .. 85 ..
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्यासंहितायां सप्तमे प्रभासखण्डे प्रथमे प्रभासक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये सोमेश्वरोत्पत्तिप्रसंगे दक्षेण स्वशापजन्ययक्ष्मरोगार्त्तस्य चंद्रस्य यक्ष्मकुष्ठरोगनिवृत्तये शिवाराधनोपदेशवर्णनंनामैकविंशोऽध्यायः .. 21 ..

16.22.s:
īśvara uvāca .. ..
dakṣeṇaivamanujñātaḥ śocankarma svakaṃ tadā ..
duḥkhaśokaparītātmā prabhāsaṃ kṣetramāgataḥ .. 1 ..
16.22.d:
ईश्वर उवाच .. ..
दक्षेणैवमनुज्ञातः शोचन्कर्म स्वकं तदा ..
दुःखशोकपरीतात्मा प्रभासं क्षेत्रमागतः .. 1 ..
16.22.m: Īśvara said: / Thus permitted by Dakṣa, grieving then over his own action, / his soul filled with sorrow and grief, he came to the sacred field of Prabhāsa.

16.22.s:
sa gatvā dakṣiṇaṃ tīraṃ sāgarasya samīpataḥ ..
dadarśa parvataṃ tatra kṛtasmaramiti śrutam .. 2 ..
16.22.d:
स गत्वा दक्षिणं तीरं सागरस्य समीपतः ..
ददर्श पर्वतं तत्र कृतस्मरमिति श्रुतम् .. 2 ..
16.22.m: Having gone near the southern shore of the ocean, / he saw there the mountain known as Kṛtasmara,

16.22.s:
yakṣavidyādharākīrṇaṃ kinnarairupaśobhitam ..
caṃdanāgurukarpūrairaśokaistilakaiḥ śubhaiḥ .. 3 ..
16.22.d:
यक्षविद्याधराकीर्णं किन्नरैरुपशोभितम् ..
चंदनागुरुकर्पूरैरशोकैस्तिलकैः शुभैः .. 3 ..
16.22.m: swarming with yakṣas and vidyādharas, adorned with kinnaras, / with sandalwood, agallochum, camphor, aśokas, and auspicious tilakas,

16.22.s:
kalhāraiḥ śatapatraiśca puṣpitaiḥ phalitaiḥ śubhaiḥ ..
āmrajambūkapitthaiśca dāḍimaiḥ panasaistathā ..4..
16.22.d:
कल्हारैः शतपत्रैश्च पुष्पितैः फलितैः शुभैः ..
आम्रजम्बूकपित्थैश्च दाडिमैः पनसैस्तथा ..4..
16.22.m: with white water-lilies and lotuses, flowering and fruiting auspiciously, / with mango, rose-apple, wood-apple, and pomegranates and jackfruits,

16.22.s:
niṃbujambīranāgaiśca kadalīkhaṃḍamaṃḍitaiḥ ..
kramukairnāgavallyādyaiḥ śālaistālaistamālakaiḥ .. 5 ..
16.22.d:
निंबुजम्बीरनागैश्च कदलीखंडमंडितैः ..
क्रमुकैर्नागवल्ल्याद्यैः शालैस्तालैस्तमालकैः .. 5 ..
16.22.m: with limes, citrons, nāgakeśaras, and adorned with groves of plantains, / with areca palms, betel vines and the like, with śālas, palmyra palms, and tamālas,

16.22.s:
bījapūrakakharjūrairdrākṣāmadhurapāṭalaiḥ ..
bilvacaṃpakatiṃdvādyaiḥ kadaṃbakakubhaistathā .. 6 ..
16.22.d:
बीजपूरकखर्जूरैर्द्राक्षामधुरपाटलैः ..
बिल्वचंपकतिंद्वाद्यैः कदंबककुभैस्तथा .. 6 ..
16.22.m: with citrons and date palms, sweet grapes and pāṭalas, / with bilvas, campakas, timburus and the like, and kadambas and arjunas,

16.22.s:
dhavāśokaśirīṣādyairnānāvṛkṣaiśca śobhitam ..
kāmaṃ kāmaphalairvṛkṣaiḥ puṣpitaiḥ phalitaiḥ śubhaiḥ .. 7 ..
16.22.d:
धवाशोकशिरीषाद्यैर्नानावृक्षैश्च शोभितम् ..
कामं कामफलैर्वृक्षैः पुष्पितैः फलितैः शुभैः .. 7 ..
16.22.m: adorned with dhavas, aśokas, śirīṣas and the like, and diverse trees, / profusely with trees yielding desired fruits, flowering, fruiting, and auspicious,

16.22.s:
haṃsakāraṃḍavākīrṇaṃ cakravākopaśobhitam ..
kokilābhiḥ śukaiścaiva nānāpakṣininādi tam .. 8 ..
16.22.d:
हंसकारंडवाकीर्णं चक्रवाकोपशोभितम् ..
कोकिलाभिः शुकैश्चैव नानापक्षिनिनादि तम् .. 8 ..
16.22.m: swarming with swans and kāraṇḍavas, adorned with cakravākas, / echoing with cuckoos, parrots, and diverse birds.

16.22.s:
jātismarāḥ pakṣiṇaśca vyājahrurmānuṣīṃ giram ..
gaṃdharvakiṃnarayugaiḥ siddhavidyādharoragaiḥ [. 9 ..
16.22.d:
जातिस्मराः पक्षिणश्च व्याजह्रुर्मानुषीं गिरम् ..
गंधर्वकिंनरयुगैः सिद्धविद्याधरोरगैः [. 9 ..
16.22.m: Birds remembering their past lives uttered human speech. / By pairs of gandharvas and kinnaras, by siddhas, vidyādharas, and uragas,

16.22.s:
krīḍadbhirvividhairdivyaiḥ śobhitaṃ parvatottamam ..
devagaṃdharvanṛtyaiśca veṇuvīṇānināditam .. 7.1.22.10 ..
16.22.d:
क्रीडद्भिर्विविधैर्दिव्यैः शोभितं पर्वतोत्तमम् ..
देवगंधर्वनृत्यैश्च वेणुवीणानिनादितम् .. 7.1.22.10 ..
16.22.m: playing in diverse celestial ways, the best of mountains was adorned, / with dances of gods and gandharvas, echoing with flutes and vīṇās,

16.22.s:
vedadhvanitaghoṣeṇa yajñahomāgnihotrajaiḥ ..
samāvṛtaṃ sarvamājyagaṃdhibhirucchritam .. 11 ..
16.22.d:
वेदध्वनितघोषेण यज्ञहोमाग्निहोत्रजैः ..
समावृतं सर्वमाज्यगंधिभिरुच्छ्रितम् .. 11 ..
16.22.m: with the resounding roar of Vedic chanting, born of sacrifices, oblations, and agnihotras, / completely enveloped, elevated, fragrant with clarified butter,

16.22.s:
śobhitaṃ carṣibhirdivyaiścāturvidyairdvijottamaiḥ ..
atriścaiva vasiṣṭhaśca pulastyaḥ pulahaḥ kratuḥ .. 12 ..
16.22.d:
शोभितं चर्षिभिर्दिव्यैश्चातुर्विद्यैर्द्विजोत्तमैः ..
अत्रिश्चैव वसिष्ठश्च पुलस्त्यः पुलहः क्रतुः .. 12 ..
16.22.m: and adorned with celestial seers, the best of brahmins versed in the four Vedas: / Atri, Vasiṣṭha, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu,

16.22.s:
bhṛguścaiva marīciśca bharadvājo'tha kaśyapaḥ ..
manuryamoṃ'girā viṣṇuḥ śātātapaparāśarau .. 13 ..
16.22.d:
भृगुश्चैव मरीचिश्च भरद्वाजोऽथ कश्यपः ..
मनुर्यमोंऽगिरा विष्णुः शातातपपराशरौ .. 13 ..
16.22.m: Bhṛgu, Marīci, Bharadvāja, and Kaśyapa, / Manu, Yama, Aṅgiras, Viṣṇu, Śātātapa, and Parāśara,

16.22.s:
āpastaṃbo'tha saṃvartaḥ kātyaḥ kātyāyano muniḥ ..
gautamaḥ śaṃkhalikhitau tathā vācaspatirmuniḥ .. 14 ..
16.22.d:
आपस्तंबोऽथ संवर्तः कात्यः कात्यायनो मुनिः ..
गौतमः शंखलिखितौ तथा वाचस्पतिर्मुनिः .. 14 ..
16.22.m: Āpastamba, Saṃvarta, Kātya, the sage Kātyāyana, / Gautama, Śaṅkha and Likhita, and the sage Vācaspati,

16.22.s:
jāmadagnyo yājñavalkya ṛṣyaśṛṃgo vibhāṃḍakaḥ ..
gārgyaśaunakadālbhyāśca vyāsa uddālakaḥ śukaḥ .. 15 ..
16.22.d:
जामदग्न्यो याज्ञवल्क्य ऋष्यशृंगो विभांडकः ..
गार्ग्यशौनकदाल्भ्याश्च व्यास उद्दालकः शुकः .. 15 ..
16.22.m: Jāmadagnya, Yājñavalkya, Ṛṣyaśṛṅga, Vibhāṇḍaka, / Gārgya, Śaunaka, Dālbhya, Vyāsa, Uddālaka, Śuka,

16.22.s:
nāradaḥ parvataścaiva durvāsā ugratāpasaḥ ..
śākalyo gālavaścaiva jābālirmudgalastathā .. 16 ..
16.22.d:
नारदः पर्वतश्चैव दुर्वासा उग्रतापसः ..
शाकल्यो गालवश्चैव जाबालिर्मुद्गलस्तथा .. 16 ..
16.22.m: Nārada, Parvata, and Durvāsas of fierce austerity, / Śākalya, Gālava, Jābāli, and Mudgala,

16.22.s:
viśvāmitraḥ kauśikaśca jahnurviśvāvasustathā ..
dhaumyaścaiva śatānando vaiśaṃpāyanajiṣṇavaḥ .. 17 ..
16.22.d:
विश्वामित्रः कौशिकश्च जह्नुर्विश्वावसुस्तथा ..
धौम्यश्चैव शतानन्दो वैशंपायनजिष्णवः .. 17 ..
16.22.m: Viśvāmitra, Kauśika, Jahnu, and Viśvāvasu, / Dhaumya, Śatānanda, Vaiśaṃpāyana, and Jiṣṇu,

16.22.s:
śākaṭāyanavārddhikyāvagniko bādarāyaṇaḥ ..
vālakhilyā mahātmāno ye ca bhūmaṇḍale sthitāḥ .. 18 ..
16.22.d:
शाकटायनवार्द्धिक्यावग्निको बादरायणः ..
वालखिल्या महात्मानो ये च भूमण्डले स्थिताः .. 18 ..
16.22.m: Śākaṭāyana, Vārddhikya, Agnika, Bādarāyaṇa, / the great-souled Vālakhilyas, and whoever dwelt upon the earth's circle—

16.22.s:
te sarve tatra tiṣṭhaṃti parvate tu kṛtasmare ..
tejasvino brahmaputrā ṛṣayo dhārmikāḥ priye .. 19 ..
16.22.d:

bhaviṣyaṃ pṛthivīśeti ādināthetyanaṃtaram .. 56 ..

भूतनाथेति घोरेति ब्रह्मेशेत्यथ नामकम् ..
भविष्यं पृथिवीशेति आदिनाथेत्यनंतरम् .. 56 ..
16.22.m: then the future names Bhūtanātha, Ghora, Brahmeśa, / Pṛthivīśa, immediately followed by Ādinātha; 56

16.22.s:
kalpeśvareti devasya caṃdranāthetyanantaram ..
nāma devasya yadbhāvi sāṃprataṃ te prakāśitam .. 57 [.
ityevamādi nāmāni svasaṃkhyātāni ṣoḍaśa ..
gatāni saṃbhaviṣyaṃti kālasyānaṃtabhāvataḥ .. 58 ..
16.22.d:
कल्पेश्वरेति देवस्य चंद्रनाथेत्यनन्तरम् ..
नाम देवस्य यद्भावि सांप्रतं ते प्रकाशितम् .. 57 [.
इत्येवमादि नामानि स्वसंख्यातानि षोडश ..
गतानि संभविष्यंति कालस्यानंतभावतः .. 58 ..
16.22.m: immediately after the god's [name] Kalpeśvara, Candranātha. / What the future name of the god will be has now been revealed to you. / These and other sixteen names, enumerated by themselves, / have passed and will come to be, because time is infinite. 57–58

16.22.s:
ekaikaṃ vartate nāma brahmaṇaḥ pralayāvadhi ..
tatonyajjāyate nāma yathā nāmānurūpataḥ .. 59 ..
16.22.d:
एकैकं वर्तते नाम ब्रह्मणः प्रलयावधि ..
ततोन्यज्जायते नाम यथा नामानुरूपतः .. 59 ..
16.22.m: Each single name endures until the dissolution of Brahmā; / after that another name arises in accordance with the proper nature of the name. 59

16.22.s:
atha kiṃ bahunoktena rahasyaṃ te prakāśitam ..
vatsa yatkāraṇeneha tapastaptaṃ tvayā'khilam ..
tanme niḥśeṣato brūhi dāsye tuṣṭo'smi te varam .. 7.1.22.60 ..
16.22.d:
अथ किं बहुनोक्तेन रहस्यं ते प्रकाशितम् ..
वत्स यत्कारणेनेह तपस्तप्तं त्वयाऽखिलम् ..
तन्मे निःशेषतो ब्रूहि दास्ये तुष्टोऽस्मि ते वरम् .. 7.1.22.60 ..
16.22.m: Now, why say much? The secret has been revealed to you. / O child, the reason for which you performed this entire austerity here, / declare that completely to me; being pleased, I will grant your boon." 60

16.22.s:
.. candra uvāca .. ..
ahaṃ śaptastu dakṣeṇa kasmiṃścitkāraṇāṃtare ..
yakṣmaṇā ca kṣayaṃ nītastasmāttvaṃ trātumarhasi .. 61 ..
16.22.d:
.. चन्द्र उवाच .. ..
अहं शप्तस्तु दक्षेण कस्मिंश्चित्कारणांतरे ..
यक्ष्मणा च क्षयं नीतस्तस्मात्त्वं त्रातुमर्हसि .. 61 ..
16.22.m: The Moon said: / "I was cursed by Dakṣa on account of a certain other reason, / and brought to consumption by pulmonary disease; therefore, you ought to rescue me." 61

16.22.s:
.. śaṃbhuruvāca .. ..
adhunā bhoḥ samaṃ paśya sarvāstā dakṣakanyakāḥ ..
kṣayaste bhavitā pakṣaṃ pakṣaṃ vṛddhirbhaviṣyati .. 62 ..
16.22.d:
.. शंभुरुवाच .. ..
अधुना भोः समं पश्य सर्वास्ता दक्षकन्यकाः ..
क्षयस्ते भविता पक्षं पक्षं वृद्धिर्भविष्यति .. 62 ..
16.22.m: Śambhu said: / "Now, look equally upon all those daughters of Dakṣa. / Your waning shall be for one fortnight, and for one fortnight there shall be waxing. 62

16.22.s:
pūrvocitāṃ prabhāṃ soma prāpsyase matprasādataḥ ..
prācetasasya dakṣasya tapasā hatapāpmanaḥ .. 63 ..
16.22.d:
पूर्वोचितां प्रभां सोम प्राप्स्यसे मत्प्रसादतः ..
प्राचेतसस्य दक्षस्य तपसा हतपाप्मनः .. 63 ..
16.22.m: You will regain your former natural luster, O Soma, through my grace; / for Dakṣa, the son of Pracetas, has destroyed his sins by austerity. 63

16.22.s:
tasyānyathā vacaḥ kartuṃ śakyaṃ nānyaiḥ surairapi ..
brāhmaṇāḥ kupitā hanyurbhasmīkuryuḥ svatejasā .. 64 ..
16.22.d:
तस्यान्यथा वचः कर्तुं शक्यं नान्यैः सुरैरपि ..
ब्राह्मणाः कुपिता हन्युर्भस्मीकुर्युः स्वतेजसा .. 64 ..
16.22.m: His word cannot be undone even by other gods. / Brahmins, when angered, can strike and turn [anything] to ashes by their own splendor; 64

16.22.s:
devānkuryuradevāṃśca nāśayeyuridaṃ jagat ..
brāhmaṇāścaiva devāśca teja ekaṃ dvidhā kṛtam .. 65 ..
16.22.d:
देवान्कुर्युरदेवांश्च नाशयेयुरिदं जगत् ..
ब्राह्मणाश्चैव देवाश्च तेज एकं द्विधा कृतम् .. 65 ..
16.22.m: they could make gods into non-gods and destroy this world. / Brahmins and gods are a single splendor divided in two: 65

16.22.s:
pratyakṣaṃ brāhmaṇā devāḥ parokṣaṃ divi devatāḥ ..
na vinā brāhmaṇā devairna devā brāhmaṇairvinā .. 66 ..
16.22.d:
प्रत्यक्षं ब्राह्मणा देवाः परोक्षं दिवि देवताः ..
न विना ब्राह्मणा देवैर्न देवा ब्राह्मणैर्विना .. 66 ..
16.22.m: the brahmins are visible gods, and the deities in heaven are invisible; / there are no brahmins without gods, nor gods without brahmins. 66

16.22.s:
ekatra mantrā stiṣṭhanti teja ekatra tiṣṭhati ..
brāhmaṇā devatā loke brāhmaṇā divi devatāḥ ..
trailokye brāhmaṇāḥ śreṣṭhā brāhmaṇā eva kāraṇam .. 67 ..
16.22.d:
एकत्र मन्त्रा स्तिष्ठन्ति तेज एकत्र तिष्ठति ..
ब्राह्मणा देवता लोके ब्राह्मणा दिवि देवताः ..
त्रैलोक्ये ब्राह्मणाः श्रेष्ठा ब्राह्मणा एव कारणम् .. 67 ..
16.22.m: Mantras abide in the one, and splendor abides in the other. / Brahmins are the deities in the world, brahmins are the deities in heaven; / brahmins are supreme in the three worlds; brahmins alone are the primary cause." 67

16.22.s:
piturniyuktāḥ pitaro bhavaṃti kriyāsu daivīṣu bhavaṃti devāḥ ..
dvijottamā hastaniṣaktatoyāstenaiva dehena bhavaṃti devāḥ .. 68 ..
16.22.d:
पितुर्नियुक्ताः पितरो भवंति क्रियासु दैवीषु भवंति देवाः ..
द्विजोत्तमा हस्तनिषक्ततोयास्तेनैव देहेन भवंति देवाः .. 68 ..
16.22.m: When appointed for the ancestors, they become the ancestors; in rites for the gods, they become the gods. / The best of the twice-born, with water poured upon their hands, become gods with that very body.

16.22.s:
ṣaṭka rmatattvābhirateṣu nityaṃ vipreṣu vedārthakutūhaleṣu ..
na teṣu bhaktyā praviśaṃti ghoraṃ mahābhayaṃ pretabhavaṃ kadācit .. 69 ..
16.22.d:
षट्क र्मतत्त्वाभिरतेषु नित्यं विप्रेषु वेदार्थकुतूहलेषु ..
न तेषु भक्त्या प्रविशंति घोरं महाभयं प्रेतभवं कदाचित् .. 69 ..
16.22.m: Through devotion to brahmins who are constantly devoted to the truth of the six ritual duties and eager for the meaning of the Vedas, / men never enter the dreadful, great terror that arises in the realm of ghosts.

16.22.s:
yadbrāhmaṇāḥ stutyatamā vadanti taddevatā karmabhirācaraṃti ..
tuṣṭeṣu tuṣṭāḥ satataṃ bhavanti pratyakṣadeveṣu parokṣadevāḥ .. 7.1.22.70 [.
yathā rudrā yathā devā maruto vasavo'śvinau ..
brahmā ca somasūryau ca tathā loke dvijottamāḥ .. 71 ..
16.22.d:
यद्ब्राह्मणाः स्तुत्यतमा वदन्ति तद्देवता कर्मभिराचरंति ..
तुष्टेषु तुष्टाः सततं भवन्ति प्रत्यक्षदेवेषु परोक्षदेवाः .. 7.1.22.70 [.
यथा रुद्रा यथा देवा मरुतो वसवोऽश्विनौ ..
ब्रह्मा च सोमसूर्यौ च तथा लोके द्विजोत्तमाः .. 71 ..
16.22.m: Whatever the brahmins, who are most worthy of praise, declare, the deities carry out through their deeds. / When the visible gods are pleased, the invisible gods are constantly pleased. / Just as the Rudras, the gods, the Maruts, the Vasus, the two Aśvins, / and Brahmā, the moon, and the sun are in heaven, so are the best of the twice-born in this world.

16.22.s:
devādhīnāḥ prajāḥ sarvā yajñādhīnāśca devatāḥ ..
te yajñā brāhmaṇādhīnāstasmāddevā dvijottamāḥ .. .. 72 ..
16.22.d:
देवाधीनाः प्रजाः सर्वा यज्ञाधीनाश्च देवताः ..
ते यज्ञा ब्राह्मणाधीनास्तस्माद्देवा द्विजोत्तमाः .. .. 72 ..
16.22.m: All subjects are dependent on the gods, and the deities are dependent on sacrifices. / Those sacrifices are dependent on brahmins; therefore, the best of the twice-born are gods.

16.22.s:
brāhmaṇānarcayennityaṃ brāhmaṇāṃstarpayetsadā ..
brāhmaṇāstārakā loke brāhmaṇātsvargamaśnute .. 73 ..
16.22.d:
ब्राह्मणानर्चयेन्नित्यं ब्राह्मणांस्तर्पयेत्सदा ..
ब्राह्मणास्तारका लोके ब्राह्मणात्स्वर्गमश्नुते .. 73 ..
16.22.m: One should daily worship brahmins; one should always satisfy brahmins. / Brahmins are saviors in this world; from a brahmin one attains heaven.

16.22.s:
abhedyamacchedyamanādimakṣayaṃ vidhiṃ purāṇaṃ paripālayanti ..
mahāmatistānabhipūjya vai dvijānbhavedajeyo divi devarāḍiva .. 79 ..
śakyaṃ hi kavacaṃ bhettuṃ nārācena śareṇa vā ..
api vajra sahasreṇa brāhmaṇāśīḥ sudurbhidā .. 75 ..
hutena śāmyate pāpaṃ hutamannena śāmyati ..
annaṃ hiraṇyadānena hiraṇyaṃ brāhmaṇāśiṣā .. 76 ..
ya icchennarakaṃ gaṃtuṃ saputrapaśubāṃdhava ..
deveṣvadhikṛtaṃ kuryādbrāhmaṇeṣu ca goṣu ca .. 77 ..
brāhmaṇāndveṣṭi yo mohāddevāngāśca makhānyadi ..
naiva tasya paro loko nā'yaṃ loko durātmanaḥ .. 78 ..
anindyā brāhmaṇā gāvaḥ kāṃcanaṃ salilaṃ striyaḥ..
pṛthivī tu ṣaḍetāni yo nindati sa pātakī ..79..
16.22.d:
अभेद्यमच्छेद्यमनादिमक्षयं विधिं पुराणं परिपालयन्ति ..
महामतिस्तानभिपूज्य वै द्विजान्भवेदजेयो दिवि देवराडिव .. 79 ..
शक्यं हि कवचं भेत्तुं नाराचेन शरेण वा ..
अपि वज्र सहस्रेण ब्राह्मणाशीः सुदुर्भिदा .. 75 ..
हुतेन शाम्यते पापं हुतमन्नेन शाम्यति ..
अन्नं हिरण्यदानेन हिरण्यं ब्राह्मणाशिषा .. 76 ..
य इच्छेन्नरकं गंतुं सपुत्रपशुबांधव ..
देवेष्वधिकृतं कुर्याद्ब्राह्मणेषु च गोषु च .. 77 ..
ब्राह्मणान्द्वेष्टि यो मोहाद्देवान्गाश्च मखान्यदि ..
नैव तस्य परो लोको नाऽयं लोको दुरात्मनः .. 78 ..
अनिन्द्या ब्राह्मणा गावः कांचनं सलिलं स्त्रियः..
पृथिवी तु षडेतानि यो निन्दति स पातकी ..79..
16.22.m:
They preserve the ancient ordinance, which is indivisible, uncuttable, beginningless, and imperishable. / Having honored those twice-born, a wise man becomes invincible in heaven like the king of gods.
Armor can indeed be pierced with an iron shaft or an arrow, / or even with a thousand thunderbolts; but a brahmin's blessing is most difficult to break.
Sin is appeased by what is offered in the fire; the offering is appeased by food; / food [is appeased] by the gift of gold, and gold by the blessing of a brahmin.
One who wishes to go to hell together with sons, cattle, and kin / should levy authority over gods, over brahmins, and over cows.
If through delusion one hates brahmins, gods, cows, and sacrifices, / that evil-minded person has neither the next world nor this world.
Brahmins, cows, gold, water, women, / and the earth: one who reviles these six is a sinner.

16.22.s:
agraṃ dharmasya rājāno mūlaṃ dharmasya brāhmaṇāḥ ..
tasmānmūlaṃ na hiṃsīta mūle hyagraṃ pratiṣṭhitam .. 7.1.22.80 ..
16.22.d:
अग्रं धर्मस्य राजानो मूलं धर्मस्य ब्राह्मणाः ..
तस्मान्मूलं न हिंसीत मूले ह्यग्रं प्रतिष्ठितम् .. 7.1.22.80 ..
16.22.m: Kings are the top of dharma; brahmins are the root of dharma. / Therefore, one must not harm the root, for the top rests upon the root.

16.22.s:
phalaṃ dharmasya rājānaḥ puṣpaṃ dharmasya brāhmaṇāḥ ..
tasmātpuṣpaṃ na hiṃsīta puṣpātsaṃjāyate phalam .. 81 ..
16.22.d:
फलं धर्मस्य राजानः पुष्पं धर्मस्य ब्राह्मणाः ..
तस्मात्पुष्पं न हिंसीत पुष्पात्संजायते फलम् .. 81 ..
16.22.m: Kings are the fruit of dharma; brahmins are the flower of dharma. / Therefore, one must not harm the flower, for the fruit is produced from the flower.

16.22.s:
rājā vṛkṣo brāhmaṇāstasya mūlaṃ paurāḥ parṇaṃ mantriṇastasya śākhāḥ ..
tasmādrājñā brāhmaṇā rakṣaṇīyā mūle gupte nāsti vṛkṣasya nāśaḥ .. 82 ..
16.22.d:
राजा वृक्षो ब्राह्मणास्तस्य मूलं पौराः पर्णं मन्त्रिणस्तस्य शाखाः ..
तस्माद्राज्ञा ब्राह्मणा रक्षणीया मूले गुप्ते नास्ति वृक्षस्य नाशः .. 82 ..
16.22.m: The king is a tree, the brahmins are its root, the citizens are the leaves, and the ministers are its branches. / Therefore, brahmins must be protected by the king; when the root is protected, there is no destruction of the tree.

16.22.s:
āsanno hi dahatyagnirdūrāddahati brāhmaṇaḥ ..
prarohatyagninā dagdhaṃ brahmadagdhaṃ na rohati .. 83 ..
16.22.d:
आसन्नो हि दहत्यग्निर्दूराद्दहति ब्राह्मणः ..
प्ररोहत्यग्निना दग्धं ब्रह्मदग्धं न रोहति .. 83 ..
16.22.m: Fire burns when near, but a brahmin burns from afar. / What is burnt by fire sprouts again; what is burnt by a brahmin does not grow.

16.22.s:
brāhmaṇānāṃ ca śāpena sarvabhakṣo hutāśanaḥ ..
samudraścāpyapeyastu viphalaśca puraṃdaraḥ .. 84 ..
16.22.d:
ब्राह्मणानां च शापेन सर्वभक्षो हुताशनः ..
समुद्रश्चाप्यपेयस्तु विफलश्च पुरंदरः .. 84 ..
16.22.m: By the curse of brahmins, the fire became an all-devourer, / the ocean became undrinkable, and Indra was rendered castrated.

16.22.s:
tvaṃ candra rājayakṣmī ca pṛthivyāmūṣarāṇi ca ..
sūryācandramasoḥ pātaḥ punaruddharaṇaṃ tayoḥ .. 85 ..
16.22.d:
त्वं चन्द्र राजयक्ष्मी च पृथिव्यामूषराणि च ..
सूर्याचन्द्रमसोः पातः पुनरुद्धरणं तयोः .. 85 ..
16.22.m: [From them came] consumption upon you, O Moon, saline barrenness on the earth, / the falling down of the sun and moon, and their rising up again;

16.22.s:
vanaspatīnāṃ niryāso dānavānāṃ parājayaḥ ..
nāgānāṃ ca vaśīkāraḥ kṣatrasyotsādanaṃ tathā ..
devotpatti viparyāso lokānāṃ ca viparyayaḥ .. 86 ..
16.22.d:
वनस्पतीनां निर्यासो दानवानां पराजयः ..
नागानां च वशीकारः क्षत्रस्योत्सादनं तथा ..
देवोत्पत्ति विपर्यासो लोकानां च विपर्ययः .. 86 ..
16.22.m: the resin of trees, the defeat of the Dānavas, / the subjugation of the serpents, the eradication of the kṣatriya order, / the reversal of the origin of the gods, and the overturning of the worlds.

16.22.s:
evamādīni tejāṃsi brāhmaṇānāṃ mahātmanām ..
tasmādvipreṣu nṛpatiḥ praṇamennityameva ca .. 87 ..
16.22.d:
एवमादीनि तेजांसि ब्राह्मणानां महात्मनाम् ..
तस्माद्विप्रेषु नृपतिः प्रणमेन्नित्यमेव च .. 87 ..
16.22.m: Such are the fiery powers of the great-souled brahmins. / Therefore, a king should always bow before the twice-born.

16.22.s:
parā mapyāpadaṃ prāpto brāhmaṇānna prakopayet ..
te hyenaṃ kupitā hanyuḥ sadyaḥ sabalavāhanam .. 88 ..
16.22.d:
परा मप्यापदं प्राप्तो ब्राह्मणान्न प्रकोपयेत् ..
ते ह्येनं कुपिता हन्युः सद्यः सबलवाहनम् .. 88 ..
16.22.m: Even when fallen into extreme calamity, he should not enrage brahmins. / For when enraged, they would instantly destroy him along with his army and vehicles.

16.22.s:
praṇītaścāpraṇītaśca yathāgnirdaivataṃ mahat ..
evaṃ vidvānavidvānvā brāhmaṇo daivataṃ mahat .. 89 ..
16.22.d:
प्रणीतश्चाप्रणीतश्च यथाग्निर्दैवतं महत् ..
एवं विद्वानविद्वान्वा ब्राह्मणो दैवतं महत् .. 89 ..
16.22.m: Just as fire, whether consecrated or unconsecrated, is a great deity, / so a brahmin, whether learned or unlearned, is a great deity.

16.22.s:
śmaśāneṣvapi tejasvī pāvako naiva duṣyati ..
hūyamānaśca yajñeṣu bhūya evābhivarddhate .. 7.1.22.90 ..
16.22.d:
श्मशानेष्वपि तेजस्वी पावको नैव दुष्यति ..
हूयमानश्च यज्ञेषु भूय एवाभिवर्द्धते .. 7.1.22.90 ..
16.22.m: Even in cremation grounds, radiant fire is not defiled at all; / and when offered into at sacrifices, it blazes forth even more.

16.22.s:
evaṃ yadyapya niṣṭeṣu varttate sarvakarmasu ..
sarveṣāṃ brāhmaṇaḥ pūjyo daivataṃ paramaṃ mahat .. 91 ..
16.22.d:
एवं यद्यप्य निष्टेषु वर्त्तते सर्वकर्मसु ..
सर्वेषां ब्राह्मणः पूज्यो दैवतं परमं महत् .. 91 ..
16.22.m: In the same way, even if he engages in all undesirable actions, / a brahmin is to be honored by all as a supreme, great deity.

16.22.s:
kṣatrasyātipravṛddhasya brāhmaṇānāṃ prabhāvataḥ ..
brāhmaṃ hi paramaṃ pūjyaṃ kṣatraṃ hi brahmasaṃbhavam .. 92 ..
16.22.d:
क्षत्रस्यातिप्रवृद्धस्य ब्राह्मणानां प्रभावतः ..
ब्राह्मं हि परमं पूज्यं क्षत्रं हि ब्रह्मसंभवम् .. 92 ..
16.22.m: Even when the kṣatriya power grows very great, by the power of brahmins [it is checked]; / for the brahmin power is supreme and worthy of honor, since the kṣatriya order originated from the brahmin.

16.22.s:
adbhyo'gnirbrahmataḥ kṣatramaśmano lohamutthitam ..
teṣāṃ sarvatragaṃ tejaḥ svāsu yoniṣu śāmyati .. 93 ..
16.22.d:
अद्भ्योऽग्निर्ब्रह्मतः क्षत्रमश्मनो लोहमुत्थितम् ..
तेषां सर्वत्रगं तेजः स्वासु योनिषु शाम्यति .. 93 ..
16.22.m: Fire arose from water, the kṣatriya from the brahmin, and iron from stone. / Their power, though effective everywhere, is calmed within their own sources.

16.22.s:
yānsamāśritya tiṣṭhanti devalokāśca sarvadā ..
brahmaiva vacanaṃ yeṣāṃ ko hiṃsyāttāñjijīviṣuḥ .. 94 ..
16.22.d:
यान्समाश्रित्य तिष्ठन्ति देवलोकाश्च सर्वदा ..
ब्रह्मैव वचनं येषां को हिंस्यात्ताञ्जिजीविषुः .. 94 ..
16.22.m: Those upon whom the worlds of the gods constantly depend, / and whose speech is the Veda itself—who that wishes to live would harm them?

16.22.s:
mriyamāṇo'pyādadīta na rājā brāhmaṇātkaram ..
na ca kṣudhā 'sya saṃsīdedbrāhmaṇo viṣaye vasan .. 95 ..
16.22.d:
म्रियमाणोऽप्याददीत न राजा ब्राह्मणात्करम् ..
न च क्षुधा ऽस्य संसीदेद्ब्राह्मणो विषये वसन् .. 95 ..
16.22.m: Even when dying, a king should not take tax from a brahmin; / nor should a brahmin living in his realm languish from hunger.

16.22.s:
yasya rājñaśca viṣaye brāhmaṇaḥ sīdati kṣudhā ..
tasya tacchatadhā rāṣṭramacirādeva sīdati .. 96 ..
16.22.d:
यस्य राज्ञश्च विषये ब्राह्मणः सीदति क्षुधा ..
तस्य तच्छतधा राष्ट्रमचिरादेव सीदति .. 96 ..
